36.m: Since many cycles of the wheel of saṃsāra / appear for embodied beings, O Acyuta, / because they are deluded by your māyā, O lord of gods, / who, dwelling in duality, can cross beyond your māyā?

36.s:
agotramasparśamarūpagandha -
manāmanirdeśamajaṃ vareṇyam .
gopendra tvāṃ yadyupāsanti dhīrā -
ste muktibhājo bhavabandhamuktāḥ .. 36.18 ..
36.d:
अगोत्रमस्पर्शमरूपगन्ध -
मनामनिर्देशमजं वरेण्यम् ।
गोपेन्द्र त्वां यद्युपासन्ति धीरा -
स्ते मुक्तिभाजो भवबन्धमुक्ताः ॥ 36.18 ॥
36.m: Having no lineage, beyond touch, formless and scentless, / beyond name and designation, unborn, to be chosen— / if the steadfast meditate on you, O lord of cattle, / they attain liberation, freed from the bondage of worldly existence.

36.s:
śabdātigaṃ vyomarūpaṃ vimūrttiṃ
vikarmmiṇāṃ śubhabhāvaṃ vareṇyam .
cakrābjapāṇiṃ tu tathopacārā-
duktaṃ purāṇe satataṃ namāmi .. 36.19 ..
36.d:
शब्दातिगं व्योमरूपं विमूर्त्तिं
विकर्म्मिणां शुभभावं वरेण्यम् ।
चक्राब्जपाणिं तु तथोपचारा-
दुक्तं पुराणे सततं नमामि ॥ 36.19 ॥
36.m: Beyond sound, whose form is space, formless, / the auspicious state for those free of actions, the one to be chosen, / yet having discus and lotus in hand by way of figurative address / as told in the Purāṇa—I constantly bow to him.

36.s:
trivikramaṃ krāntajagattrayaṃ ca
caturmūrttiṃ viśvagatāṃ kṣitīśam .
śambhuṃ vibhuṃ bhūtapatiṃ sureśaṃ
namāmyahaṃ viṣṇumanantamūrttim .. 36.20 ..
36.d:
त्रिविक्रमं क्रान्तजगत्त्रयं च
चतुर्मूर्त्तिं विश्वगतां क्षितीशम् ।
शम्भुं विभुं भूतपतिं सुरेशं
नमाम्यहं विष्णुमनन्तमूर्त्तिम् ॥ 36.20 ॥
36.m: To Trivikrama, who strode across the three worlds, / possessing four forms, pervasive in the universe, the lord of the earth, / the benevolent, the all-pervading, the lord of beings, the lord of gods, / I bow to Viṣṇu of endless forms.

36.s:
tvaṃ deva sarvāṇi carācarāṇi
sṛjasyatho saṃharase tvameva .
māṃ muktikāmaṃ naya deva śīghraṃ
yasmin gatā yogino nāpayānti .. 36.21 ..
36.d:
त्वं देव सर्वाणि चराचराणि
सृजस्यथो संहरसे त्वमेव ।
मां मुक्तिकामं नय देव शीघ्रं
यस्मिन् गता योगिनो नापयान्ति ॥ 36.21 ॥
36.m: You, O God, create all things moving and unmoving, / and you alone dissolve them. / Lead me swiftly, O God, desiring liberation, / to that [abode] having gone whereto yogins never depart.

36.s:
jayasva govinda mahānubhāva
jayasva viṣṇo jaya padmanābha .
jayasva sarvajña jayāprameya
jayasva viśveśvara viśvamūrtte .. 36.22 ..
36.d:
जयस्व गोविन्द महानुभाव
जयस्व विष्णो जय पद्मनाभ ।
जयस्व सर्वज्ञ जयाप्रमेय
जयस्व विश्वेश्वर विश्वमूर्त्ते ॥ 36.22 ॥
36.m: Be victorious, Govinda of great majesty! / Be victorious, O Viṣṇu! Victory, O Padmanābha! / Be victorious, O all-knowing one! Victory, O immeasurable one! / Be victorious, O lord of the universe, whose form is the universe!

36.s:
śrīvarāha uvāca .
evaṃ stutvā tadā rājā nidhāya svaṃ kalevaram .
paramātmani govinde layamāgācca śāśvate .. 36.23 ..
36.d:
श्रीवराह उवाच ।
एवं स्तुत्वा तदा राजा निधाय स्वं कलेवरम् ।
परमात्मनि गोविन्दे लयमागाच्च शाश्वते ॥ 36.23 ॥
36.m: The venerable Varāha said: / Having thus praised him, the king then cast off his own body / and attained dissolution in the eternal supreme self, Govinda.

36.s: .. iti śrīvarāhapurāṇe bhagavacchāstre ṣaṭtriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 36 ..
36.d: ॥ इति श्रीवराहपुराणे भगवच्छास्त्रे षट्त्रिंशोऽध्यायः ॥ 36 ॥
36.m: Thus ends the thirty-sixth chapter in the venerable Varāha Purāṇa, the scripture of the Lord.

37.s:
dharaṇyuvāca .
kathamārādhyase deva bhaktimadbhirnarairvibho .
strībhirvā sarvametanme śaṃsa tvaṃ bhūtabhāvana .. 37.1 ..
37.d:
धरण्युवाच ।
कथमाराध्यसे देव भक्तिमद्भिर्नरैर्विभो ।
स्त्रीभिर्वा सर्वमेतन्मे शंस त्वं भूतभावन ॥ 37.1 ॥
37.m: Dharaṇī said: / How are you worshipped, O God, by devoted men, / O all-pervading lord, or by women? Declare all this to me, O creator of beings!

37.s:
śrīvarāha uvāca .
bhāvasādhyo'smyahaṃ devi na vittairna japairaham .
sādhyastathā'pi bhaktānāṃ kāyakleśaṃ vadāmi te .. 37.2 ..
37.d:
श्रीवराह उवाच ।
भावसाध्योऽस्म्यहं देवि न वित्तैर्न जपैरहम् ।
साध्यस्तथाऽपि भक्तानां कायक्लेशं वदामि ते ॥ 37.2 ॥
37.m: The venerable Varāha said: / I am to be attained through inner feeling, O goddess, not through wealth nor through recitations / am I to be attained; nevertheless, I shall tell you of the bodily exertion of devotees.

37.s:
karmaṇā manasā vācā maccitto yo naro bhavet .
tasya vratāni dhāsyāmi vividhāni nibodha me .. 37.3 ..
37.d:
कर्मणा मनसा वाचा मच्चित्तो यो नरो भवेत् ।
तस्य व्रतानि धास्यामि विविधानि निबोध मे ॥ 37.3 ॥
37.m: The human being whose mind is set on me in deed, thought, and speech— / for him I shall establish various observances; learn of them from me.

37.s:
ahiṃsā satyamasteyaṃ brahmacaryaṃ prakīrtitam (-kalkata)ā .
etāni mānasānyāhurvratāni tu dharādhare .. 37.4 ..
37.d:
अहिंसा सत्यमस्तेयं ब्रह्मचर्यं प्रकीर्तितम् (-कल्कत)आ ।
एतानि मानसान्याहुर्व्रतानि तु धराधरे ॥ 37.4 ॥
37.m: Non-violence, truthfulness, non-stealing, and celibacy are celebrated— / these they call mental observances, O supporter of the earth.

37.s:
ekabhaktaṃ tathā naktamupavāsādikaṃ ca yat .
tatsarvaṃ kāyikaṃ puṃsāṃ vrataṃ bhavati nānyathā .. 37.5 ..
37.d:
एकभक्तं तथा नक्तमुपवासादिकं च यत् ।
तत्सर्वं कायिकं पुंसां व्रतं भवति नान्यथा ॥ 37.5 ॥
37.m: Eating once a day, eating only at night, and fasting and the like— / all that is the physical observance of men, not otherwise.

37.s:
maunaṃ cādhyayanaṃ caiva devastutyarthakīrtitat .
nivṛttiścāpi paiśunyād vācikaṃ vratamuttamam ..37.6 ..
37.d:
मौनं चाध्ययनं चैव देवस्तुत्यर्थकीर्तितत् ।
निवृत्तिश्चापि पैशुन्याद् वाचिकं व्रतमुत्तमम् ॥37.6 ॥
37.m: Silence, study [of scripture], praise of God for the sake of [reciting] meaning, / and refraining from slander is the supreme vocal observance.

37.s:
atrāpi śrūyate cānyadṛṣirugratapāḥ purā .
brahmaputraḥ purā kalpe āruṇirnāma nāmataḥ .. 37.7 ..
37.d:
अत्रापि श्रूयते चान्यदृषिरुग्रतपाः पुरा ।
ब्रह्मपुत्रः पुरा कल्पे आरुणिर्नाम नामतः ॥ 37.7 ॥
37.m: In this connection another [story] is also heard of a sage of fierce austerities in former times, / a son of Brahmā in a previous kalpa, Āruṇi by name.

37.s:
so'raṇyamagamat kiṃcit taporthī dvijasattamaḥ .
tapastepe tatastasminnupavāsaparāyaṇaḥ .. 37.8 ..
37.d:
सोऽरण्यमगमत् किंचित् तपोर्थी द्विजसत्तमः ।
तपस्तेपे ततस्तस्मिन्नुपवासपरायणः ॥ 37.8 ॥
37.m: Desiring austerities, that best of twice-born went to a certain forest; / then he performed tapas therein, devoted to fasting.

37.s:
devikāyāstaṭe ramye so'vasad brāhmaṇaḥ kila .
kadācidabhiṣekāya sa jagāma mahānadīm .. 37.9 ..
37.d:
देविकायास्तटे रम्ये सोऽवसद् ब्राह्मणः किल ।
कदाचिदभिषेकाय स जगाम महानदीम् ॥ 37.9 ॥
37.m: On the delightful bank of the Devikā, that brāhmaṇa indeed resided; / once he went to the great river for a ceremonial bath.

37.s:
tatra snātvā japan vipro dadarśāyāntamagrataḥ .
vyādhaṃ mahādhanuḥpāṇimugranetraṃ vibhīṣaṇam .. 37.10 ..
37.d:
तत्र स्नात्वा जपन् विप्रो ददर्शायान्तमग्रतः ।
व्याधं महाधनुःपाणिमुग्रनेत्रं विभीषणम् ॥ 37.10 ॥
37.m: Having bathed there, murmuring prayers, the vipra saw approaching before him / a hunter with a great bow in hand, of fierce eyes, terrifying.

37.s:
taṃ dvijaṃ hantumāyāt sa valkalānāṃ jighṛkṣayā .
taṃ dṛṣṭvā kṣubhito vipro brahmaghnasya bhayāditi .
dhyāyan nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ tasthau tatraiva sa dvijaḥ .. 37.11 ..
37.d:
तं द्विजं हन्तुमायात् स वल्कलानां जिघृक्षया ।
तं दृष्ट्वा क्षुभितो विप्रो ब्रह्मघ्नस्य भयादिति ।
ध्यायन् नारायणं देवं तस्थौ तत्रैव स द्विजः ॥ 37.11 ॥
37.m: He came to kill that twice-born out of a desire to seize his bark garments. / Seeing him, the vipra became agitated out of fear of that killer of brāhmaṇas; / meditating upon God Nārāyaṇa, that twice-born stood right there.

37.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā'ntargatahariṃ vyādho bhīta ivāgrataḥ .
vihāya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ tato vacanamabravīt .. 37.12 ..
37.d:
तं दृष्ट्वाऽन्तर्गतहरिं व्याधो भीत इवाग्रतः ।
विहाय सशरं चापं ततो वचनमब्रवीत् ॥ 37.12 ॥
37.m: Seeing Hari within him, the hunter, as if terrified before him, / cast down his bow along with arrows and then spoke these words:

37.s:
vyādha uvāca .
hantumicchurahaṃ brahman bhavantaṃ prāgihāgataḥ .
idānīṃ darśanāt tubhyaṃ sā matiḥ kvāpi me gatā .. 37.13 ..
37.d:
व्याध उवाच ।
हन्तुमिच्छुरहं ब्रह्मन् भवन्तं प्रागिहागतः ।
इदानीं दर्शनात् तुभ्यं सा मतिः क्वापि मे गता ॥ 37.13 ॥
37.m: The hunter said: / Wishing to kill you, O brāhmaṇa, I came here previously; / now, from the sight of you, that intention of mine has vanished somewhere.

37.s:
brāhmaṇānāṃ sahastrāṇi sastrīṇāmayutāni ca .
nihatāni mayā brahman nihatau ca kuṭambinau .. 37.14 ..
37.d:
ब्राह्मणानां सहस्त्राणि सस्त्रीणामयुतानि च ।
निहतानि मया ब्रह्मन् निहतौ च कुटम्बिनौ ॥ 37.14 ॥
37.m: Thousands of brāhmaṇas and myriads of them along with women / have been killed by me, O brāhmaṇa, and two householders were slain.

37.s:
narake'bhyadhikaṃ cittaṃ kadācidapi vidyate .
idānīṃ taptumicchāmi tapo'haṃ tvatsamīpataḥ .
upadeśapradānena prasādaṃ kartumarhasi .. 37.15 ..
37.d:
नरकेऽभ्यधिकं चित्तं कदाचिदपि विद्यते ।
इदानीं तप्तुमिच्छामि तपोऽहं त्वत्समीपतः ।
उपदेशप्रदानेन प्रसादं कर्तुमर्हसि ॥ 37.15 ॥
37.m: My mind is ever intensely set upon hell. / Now I wish to perform tapas near you; / you should grant your favor by giving instruction.

37.s:
evamukto'pyasau vipro nottaraṃ pratyapadyata .
brahmahā pāpakarmeti matvā brāhmaṇapuṃgavaḥ .. 37.16 ..
37.d:
एवमुक्तोऽप्यसौ विप्रो नोत्तरं प्रत्यपद्यत ।
ब्रह्महा पापकर्मेति मत्वा ब्राह्मणपुंगवः ॥ 37.16 ॥
37.m: Though addressed in this way, that vipra made no answer, / considering, 'He is a slayer of a brāhmaṇa, an evil-doer,' that bull among brāhmaṇas.

37.s:
anukto'pi sa dharmepsurvyādhastatraiva tasthivān .
snātvā nadyāṃ dvijaḥ so'pi vṛkṣamūlamupāśritaḥ .. 37.17 ..
37.d:
अनुक्तोऽपि स धर्मेप्सुर्व्याधस्तत्रैव तस्थिवान् ।
स्नात्वा नद्यां द्विजः सोऽपि वृक्षमूलमुपाश्रितः ॥ 37.17 ॥
37.m: Even though unaddressed, that hunter, desiring righteousness, remained right there; / and that twice-born, having bathed in the river, resorted to the foot of a tree.

37.s:
kasyacit tvatha kālasya tāṃ nadīmagamat kila .
vyāghro bubhukṣitaḥ śāntaṃ taṃ vipraṃ hantumudyataḥ .. 37.18 ..
37.d:
कस्यचित् त्वथ कालस्य तां नदीमगमत् किल ।
व्याघ्रो बुभुक्षितः शान्तं तं विप्रं हन्तुमुद्यतः ॥ 37.18 ॥
37.m: Then, after some time, a hungry tiger indeed / went to that river, intent on killing that peaceful vipra.

37.s:
antarjalagataṃ vipraṃ yāvad vyāghro jighṛkṣati .
tāvad vyādhena viddho'sau sadyaḥ prāṇairviyojitaḥ .. 37.19 ..
37.d:
अन्तर्जलगतं विप्रं यावद् व्याघ्रो जिघृक्षति ।
तावद् व्याधेन विद्धोऽसौ सद्यः प्राणैर्वियोजितः ॥ 37.19 ॥
37.m: Just as the tiger sought to seize the vipra submerged in the water, / he was pierced by the hunter and instantly separated from his vital breaths.

37.s:
tasmād vyāghraśarīrāt tu utthāya puruṣaḥ kila .
vipraścāntarjale magnaḥ śrutvā taṃ śabdamākulam .
namo nārāyaṇāyeti vākyamuccairuvāca ha .. 37.20 ..
37.d:
तस्माद् व्याघ्रशरीरात् तु उत्थाय पुरुषः किल ।
विप्रश्चान्तर्जले मग्नः श्रुत्वा तं शब्दमाकुलम् ।
नमो नारायणायेति वाक्यमुच्चैरुवाच ह ॥ 37.20 ॥
37.m: Indeed, rising up from that tiger's body, a man [appeared]; / and the vipra, submerged in the water, hearing that agitated sound, / spoke aloud the words: "Obeisance to Nārāyaṇa!"

37.s:
vyāghreṇāpi śruto mantraḥ prāṇaiḥ kaṇṭhasthitaistataḥ .
śrutamātre jahau prāṇān puruṣaścābhavacchubhaḥ .. 37.21 ..
37.d:
व्याघ्रेणापि श्रुतो मन्त्रः प्राणैः कण्ठस्थितैस्ततः ।
श्रुतमात्रे जहौ प्राणान् पुरुषश्चाभवच्छुभः ॥ 37.21 ॥
37.m: The mantra was heard even by the tiger, with his vital breaths held in his throat; / immediately upon hearing it he gave up his life, and became an auspicious man.

37.s:
so'bravīd yāmi taṃ deśaṃ yatra viṣṇuḥ sanātanaḥ .
tvatprasādād dvijaśreṣṭha muktapāpmā nirāmayaḥ .. 37.22 ..
37.d:
सोऽब्रवीद् यामि तं देशं यत्र विष्णुः सनातनः ।
त्वत्प्रसादाद् द्विजश्रेष्ठ मुक्तपाप्मा निरामयः ॥ 37.22 ॥
37.m: He said: "By your grace, O best of the twice-born, freed from sin and without affliction, / I go to that realm where eternal Viṣṇu resides."

37.s:
ityukto brāhmaṇaḥ prāha ko'si tvaṃ puruṣarṣabha .
so'bravīt tasya rājendraḥ pratāpī pūrvajanmani .
dīrghabāhuriti khyātaḥ sarvadharmaviśāradaḥ .. 37.23 ..
37.d:
इत्युक्तो ब्राह्मणः प्राह कोऽसि त्वं पुरुषर्षभ ।
सोऽब्रवीत् तस्य राजेन्द्रः प्रतापी पूर्वजन्मनि ।
दीर्घबाहुरिति ख्यातः सर्वधर्मविशारदः ॥ 37.23 ॥
37.m: Addressed thus, the brāhmaṇa said: "Who are you, O bull among men?" / He replied to him: "In a former birth, [I was] a powerful king of kings / known as Dīrghabāhu, skilled in all righteousness.

37.s:
ahaṃ jānāmi vedāṃśca ahaṃ vedmi śubhāśubham .
brāhmaṇe naiva me kāryaṃ kiṃ vastu brāhmaṇā iti .. 37.24 ..
37.d:
अहं जानामि वेदांश्च अहं वेद्मि शुभाशुभम् ।
ब्राह्मणे नैव मे कार्यं किं वस्तु ब्राह्मणा इति ॥ 37.24 ॥
37.m: I said: 'I know the Vedas, and I know what is auspicious and inauspicious; / I have no need of a brāhmaṇa; what entity are brāhmaṇas?'

37.s:
tasyaivaṃ vādino viprāḥ sarve krodhasamanvitāḥ .
ūcuḥ śāpaṃ durādharṣaḥ krūro vyāghro bhaviṣyasi .. 37.25 ..
37.d:
तस्यैवं वादिनो विप्राः सर्वे क्रोधसमन्विताः ।
ऊचुः शापं दुराधर्षः क्रूरो व्याघ्रो भविष्यसि ॥ 37.25 ॥
37.m: As he spoke thus, all the vipras, filled with anger, / pronounced a curse: 'You shall become a cruel, unassailable tiger!

37.s:
avamānāt tu viprāṇāṃ satyāntaṃ smaraṇaṃ tava .
mṛtyukālena saṃmūḍha keśavena bhaviṣyati .. 37.26 ..
37.d:
अवमानात् तु विप्राणां सत्यान्तं स्मरणं तव ।
मृत्युकालेन संमूढ केशवेन भविष्यति ॥ 37.26 ॥
37.m: Because of your disrespect toward vipras, O fool, / your memory shall last until death, [brought to an end] through Keśava.'

37.s:
ityukto'haṃ purā taistu brāhmaṇairvedapāragaiḥ .
tameva sarvaṃ saṃprāpto brahmaśāpaṃ supuṣkalam .. 37.27 ..
37.d:
इत्युक्तोऽहं पुरा तैस्तु ब्राह्मणैर्वेदपारगैः ।
तमेव सर्वं संप्राप्तो ब्रह्मशापं सुपुष्कलम् ॥ 37.27 ॥
37.m: Having been spoken to thus in the past by those brāhmaṇas who had crossed to the end of the Vedas, / I incurred that very full curse of the brāhmaṇas.

37.s:
tataste brāhmaṇā sarve praṇipatya mahāmune .
uktā'nugrahahetorvai ūcuste māmimaṃ purā .. 37.28 ..
37.d:
ततस्ते ब्राह्मणा सर्वे प्रणिपत्य महामुने ।
उक्ताऽनुग्रहहेतोर्वै ऊचुस्ते मामिमं पुरा ॥ 37.28 ॥
37.m: Then, having bowed down to all those brāhmaṇas, O great sage, / and having addressed them for the sake of mercy, they spoke this to me in the past:

37.s:
ṣaṣṭhānnakālikasyāgre yaste sthāsyati kaścana .
sa bhakṣyaste tu bhavitā kaṃcitkālaṃ narādhama .. 37.29 ..
37.d:
षष्ठान्नकालिकस्याग्रे यस्ते स्थास्यति कश्चन ।
स भक्ष्यस्ते तु भविता कंचित्कालं नराधम ॥ 37.29 ॥
37.m: 'Whoever stands before you at the time of your sixth meal, / he shall be your food for some time, O lowest of men.

37.s:
yadeṣughātaṃ labdhvā tu prāṇaiḥ kaṇṭhagatairbhavān .
śroṣyase dvijavaktrāt tu namo nārāyaṇeti hi .
tadā svargagatistubhyaṃ bhavitā nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 37.30 ..
37.d:
यदेषुघातं लब्ध्वा तु प्राणैः कण्ठगतैर्भवान् ।
श्रोष्यसे द्विजवक्त्रात् तु नमो नारायणेति हि ।
तदा स्वर्गगतिस्तुभ्यं भविता नात्र संशयः ॥ 37.30 ॥
37.m: When, having received the blow of an arrow, with your life-breaths in your throat, / you hear from the mouth of a twice-born, "Obeisance to Nārāyaṇa," / then your departure to heaven will occur; there is no doubt here.'

37.s:
paravaktragatasyāpi viṣṇornāma śrutaṃ mayā .
labdhadveṣasya viprāṇāṃ pratyakṣaṃ tava sattama .. 37.31 ..
37.d:
परवक्त्रगतस्यापि विष्णोर्नाम श्रुतं मया ।
लब्धद्वेषस्य विप्राणां प्रत्यक्षं तव सत्तम ॥ 37.31 ॥
37.m: Even though uttered from another's mouth, the name of Viṣṇu was heard by me, / who had incurred the hatred of vipras, before your very eyes, O best of beings.

37.s:
yaḥ punarbrāhmaṇān pūjya svavaktreṇa namo harim .
vadan prāṇaṃ vimucyeta muktau'sau vītakilbiṣaḥ ... 37.32 ..
37.d:
यः पुनर्ब्राह्मणान् पूज्य स्ववक्त्रेण नमो हरिम् ।
वदन् प्राणं विमुच्येत मुक्तौऽसौ वीतकिल्बिषः ॥। 37.32 ॥
37.m: How much more, then, one who, having honored brāhmaṇas, releases his life / with his own mouth saying 'Obeisance to Hari'; he is liberated, freed from taint.

37.s:
satyaṃ satyaṃ punaḥ satyamutkṣipya bhujamucyate .
jaṅgamā brāhmaṇā devāḥ kūṭasthaḥ puruṣottamaḥ .. 37.33 ..
37.d:
सत्यं सत्यं पुनः सत्यमुत्क्षिप्य भुजमुच्यते ।
जङ्गमा ब्राह्मणा देवाः कूटस्थः पुरुषोत्तमः ॥ 37.33 ॥
37.m: Raising my arm, it is proclaimed: Truth, truth, and again truth! / The brāhmaṇas are walking deities; the Highest Person is the immovable rock.

37.s:
evamuktvā gataḥ svargaṃ sa rājā vītakalmaṣaḥ .
brāhmaṇo'pi sadāyuktastaṃ vyādhaṃ pratyabhāṣata .. 37.34 ..
37.d:
एवमुक्त्वा गतः स्वर्गं स राजा वीतकल्मषः ।
ब्राह्मणोऽपि सदायुक्तस्तं व्याधं प्रत्यभाषत ॥ 37.34 ॥
37.m: Having spoken thus, that king, freed from stain, went to heaven. / The brāhmaṇa too, ever disciplined, addressed that hunter.

37.s:
ṛṣiruvāca .
jighṛkṣormṛgarājasya yattvayā rakṣito hyaham .
tatputra tuṣṭaste dadmi varaṃ varaya suvrata .. 37.35 ..
37.d:
ऋषिरुवाच ।
जिघृक्षोर्मृगराजस्य यत्त्वया रक्षितो ह्यहम् ।
तत्पुत्र तुष्टस्ते दद्मि वरं वरय सुव्रत ॥ 37.35 ॥
37.m: The sage said: / Because I was indeed protected by you from the king of beasts wishing to seize me, / therefore, son, I am pleased; I grant you a boon; choose a boon, O one of good vows.

37.s:
vyādha uvāca .
eṣa eva varo mahyaṃ yat tvaṃ māṃ bhāṣase dvija .
ataḥ paraṃ vareṇāhaṃ kiṃ karomi praśādhi mām .. 37.36 ..
37.d:
व्याध उवाच ।
एष एव वरो मह्यं यत् त्वं मां भाषसे द्विज ।
अतः परं वरेणाहं किं करोमि प्रशाधि माम् ॥ 37.36 ॥
37.m: The hunter said: / This itself is the boon for me, that you speak to me, O twice-born. / What shall I do with a boon beyond this? Instruct me!

37.s:
ṛṣiruvāca .
ahaṃ tvayā purā putra prārthito'smi tapo'rthinā .
bahupātakayuktena ghorarūpeṇa cānagha .. 37.37 ..
37.d:
ऋषिरुवाच ।
अहं त्वया पुरा पुत्र प्रार्थितोऽस्मि तपोऽर्थिना ।
बहुपातकयुक्तेन घोररूपेण चानघ ॥ 37.37 ॥
37.m: The sage said: / Formerly, son, I was solicited by you, who were desirous of asceticism, / endowed with many sins, and of terrible appearance, O sinless one.

37.s:
idānīṃ tava pāpāni devikābhiṣaveṇa ca .
maddarśanena ca ciraṃ viṣṇunāmaśrutena ca .
naṣṭāni śuddhadeho'si sāṃprataṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 37.38 ..
37.d:
इदानीं तव पापानि देविकाभिषवेण च ।
मद्दर्शनेन च चिरं विष्णुनामश्रुतेन च ।
नष्टानि शुद्धदेहोऽसि सांप्रतं नात्र संशयः ॥ 37.38 ॥
37.m: Now your sins have been destroyed by bathing in the Devikā, / by the sight of me, and by having heard the name of Viṣṇu for a long time; / your body is pure at present; there is no doubt of this.

37.s:
idānīṃ varamekaṃ tvaṃ gṛhāṇa mama sannidhau .
tapaḥ kuruṣva sādho tvaṃ cirakālaṃ yadīcchasi .. 37.39 ..
37.d:
इदानीं वरमेकं त्वं गृहाण मम सन्निधौ ।
तपः कुरुष्व साधो त्वं चिरकालं यदीच्छसि ॥ 37.39 ॥
37.m: Now receive one boon in my presence: / perform asceticism, O virtuous one, for a long time if you wish.

37.s:
vyādha uvāca .
ya eṣa bhavatā prokto viṣṇurnārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ .
sa kathaṃ prāpyate martyaireṣa eva varo mama .. 37.40 ..
37.d:
व्याध उवाच ।
य एष भवता प्रोक्तो विष्णुर्नारायणः प्रभुः ।
स कथं प्राप्यते मर्त्यैरेष एव वरो मम ॥ 37.40 ॥
37.m: The hunter said: / This Lord Viṣṇu Nārāyaṇa who has been spoken of by you— / how is he to be attained by mortals? This alone is my boon.

37.s:
ṛṣiruvāca .
tamuddiśya vrataṃ kuryād yatkiṃcitpuruṣo'cyutam .
sa paraṃ tamavāpnoti bhaktayā yuktaḥ pumāniti .. 37.41 ..
37.d:
ऋषिरुवाच ।
तमुद्दिश्य व्रतं कुर्याद् यत्किंचित्पुरुषोऽच्युतम् ।
स परं तमवाप्नोति भक्तया युक्तः पुमानिति ॥ 37.41 ॥
37.m: The sage said: / Whatever vow a man performs directed toward that Acyuta, / endowed with devotion, that man attains that Supreme [State].

37.s:
evaṃ jñātvā bhavān putra vratametat samācara .
na bhakṣayed gaṇānnaṃ tu na vadedanṛtaṃ kvacit .. 37.42 ..
37.d:
एवं ज्ञात्वा भवान् पुत्र व्रतमेतत् समाचर ।
न भक्षयेद् गणान्नं तु न वदेदनृतं क्वचित् ॥ 37.42 ॥
37.m: Knowing this, son, observe this vow: / one should not eat food offered by a group, nor should one ever speak falsehood.

37.s:
etat te vratamādiṣṭaṃ mayā vyādhavara dhruvam .
atraivaṃ tapasā yuktastiṣṭha tvaṃ yāvadicchasi .. 37.43 ..
37.d:
एतत् ते व्रतमादिष्टं मया व्याधवर ध्रुवम् ।
अत्रैवं तपसा युक्तस्तिष्ठ त्वं यावदिच्छसि ॥ 37.43 ॥
37.m: This vow has been enjoined upon you firmly by me, O best of hunters. / Remaining here, endowed with asceticism, stay as long as you wish.

37.s:
śrīvarāha uvāca .
evaṃ cintānvitaṃ matvā varado brāhmaṇo'bhavat .
mokṣārthinamatho buddhvā vañcayitvā gato muniḥ .. 37.44 ..
37.d:
श्रीवराह उवाच ।
एवं चिन्तान्वितं मत्वा वरदो ब्राह्मणोऽभवत् ।
मोक्षार्थिनमथो बुद्ध्वा वञ्चयित्वा गतो मुनिः ॥ 37.44 ॥
37.m: The glorious Varāha said: / Seeing him thus filled with thought, the brāhmaṇa became a grantor of boons; / then, knowing him to be a seeker of liberation, the sage deceived him and departed.

37.s: .. iti śrīvarāhapurāṇe bhagavacchāstre saptatriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 37 ..
37.d: ॥ इति श्रीवराहपुराणे भगवच्छास्त्रे सप्तत्रिंशोऽध्यायः ॥ 37 ॥
37.m: Thus ends the thirty-seventh chapter in the venerable Varāha Purāṇa, a sacred scripture of the Lord.

38.s:
śrīvarāha uvāca .
sa śubhaṃ śobhanaṃ mārgamāsthāya vyādhasattamaḥ .
tapastepe nirāhārastaṃ guruṃ manasā smaran .. 38.1 ..
38.d:
श्रीवराह उवाच ।
स शुभं शोभनं मार्गमास्थाय व्याधसत्तमः ।
तपस्तेपे निराहारस्तं गुरुं मनसा स्मरन् ॥ 38.1 ॥
38.m: The glorious Varāha said: / Having resorted to that auspicious and lovely path, the best of hunters / performed asceticism without food, remembering that guru in his mind.

38.s:
bhikṣākāle tu saṃprāpte śīrṇaparṇānyabhakṣayat .
sa kadācit kṣudhāviṣṭo vṛkṣamūlaṃ samāśritaḥ .. 38.2 ..
38.d:
भिक्षाकाले तु संप्राप्ते शीर्णपर्णान्यभक्षयत् ।
स कदाचित् क्षुधाविष्टो वृक्षमूलं समाश्रितः ॥ 38.2 ॥
38.m: When the time for begging food arrived, he ate withered leaves. / Once, overcome with hunger, he took refuge at the foot of a tree.

38.s:
bubhukṣitastaroḥ parṇamaicchad bhakṣitumantikāt .
ityevaṃ kurvato vyomni vāguvācāśarīriṇī .. 38.3 ..
38.d:
बुभुक्षितस्तरोः पर्णमैच्छद् भक्षितुमन्तिकात् ।
इत्येवं कुर्वतो व्योम्नि वागुवाचाशरीरिणी ॥ 38.3 ॥
38.m: Hungry, he wished to eat a leaf from near the tree. / As he was doing so, a bodiless voice in the sky spoke:

38.s:
mā bhakṣayasva sakaṭamuccairevaṃ prabhāṣite .
tato'sau taṃ vihāyānyad vārkṣaṃ patitamagrahīt .. 38.4 ..
38.d:
मा भक्षयस्व सकटमुच्चैरेवं प्रभाषिते ।
ततोऽसौ तं विहायान्यद् वार्क्षं पतितमग्रहीत् ॥ 38.4 ॥
38.m: "Do not eat Sakaṭa!" When this was loudly uttered, / he then left it and took another fallen from the tree.

38.s:
tamapyevaṃ niṣiddhaṃ syādanyaṃ tathaivameva ca .
evaṃ sa sakaṭaṃ matvā vyādhaḥ kiñcinna bhakṣayat .. 38.5 ..
38.d:
तमप्येवं निषिद्धं स्यादन्यं तथैवमेव च ।
एवं स सकटं मत्वा व्याधः किञ्चिन्न भक्षयत् ॥ 38.5 ॥
38.m: That one also was forbidden in the same way, and another in that very manner; / thinking in this way, 'It is Sakaṭa,' the hunter ate nothing at all.

38.s:
nirāhārastapastepe smaran gurumatandritaḥ .
tasyātha bahunā kāle gate ṛṣivaro'bhyagāt .. 38.6 ..
38.d:
निराहारस्तपस्तेपे स्मरन् गुरुमतन्द्रितः ।
तस्याथ बहुना काले गते ऋषिवरोऽभ्यगात् ॥ 38.6 ॥
38.m: Without food, unwearied, he performed asceticism remembering his guru. / Then, when a long time had passed for him, an excellent sage arrived.

38.s:
durvāsāḥ śaṃsitātmā vai kiñcitprāṇamapaśyata .
vyādhaṃ tapotthatejobhirjvalamānaṃ haviryathā .. 38.7 ..
38.d:
दुर्वासाः शंसितात्मा वै किञ्चित्प्राणमपश्यत ।
व्याधं तपोत्थतेजोभिर्ज्वलमानं हविर्यथा ॥ 38.7 ॥
38.m: Durvāsas, whose self was praised, saw the hunter, with only a little breath left, / blazing like a sacrificial oblation with the splendors born of his asceticism.

38.s:
so'pi vyādhastu taṃ natvā śirasā'tha mahāmunim .
uvāca sa kṛtārtho'smi bhagavan darśanāt tava .. 38.8 ..
38.d:
सोऽपि व्याधस्तु तं नत्वा शिरसाऽथ महामुनिम् ।
उवाच स कृतार्थोऽस्मि भगवन् दर्शनात् तव ॥ 38.8 ॥
38.m: Then that hunter too, having bowed to that great sage with his head, / said: "I have accomplished my purpose, O Lord, through the sight of you.

38.s:
idānīṃ śrāddhakālaṃ me prāptaṃ tvamavadhāraya .
śīrṇaparṇāni bhakṣayan vai tairevāhaṃ mahāmune .
bhavantaṃ prīṇayāmīti vyādhastaṃ vākyamabravīt .. 38.9 ..
38.d:
इदानीं श्राद्धकालं मे प्राप्तं त्वमवधारय ।
शीर्णपर्णानि भक्षयन् वै तैरेवाहं महामुने ।
भवन्तं प्रीणयामीति व्याधस्तं वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥ 38.9 ॥
38.m: Understand that the time for my offering to the ancestors has now arrived; / indeed, eating withered leaves, with those very leaves, O great sage, / I shall gratify you." Thus the hunter spoke the word to him.

38.s:
durvāsā api taṃ śuddhaṃ śuddhabhāvaṃ jitendriyam .
jijñāsustattapo vākyamidamuccairuvāca ha .. 38.10 ..
38.d:
दुर्वासा अपि तं शुद्धं शुद्धभावं जितेन्द्रियम् ।
जिज्ञासुस्तत्तपो वाक्यमिदमुच्चैरुवाच ह ॥ 38.10 ॥
38.m: Durvāsas also, wishing to test that asceticism of his— / he who was pure, of pure disposition, and had conquered his senses—spoke these words aloud:

38.s:
yavagodhūmaśālīnāmannaṃ caiva susaṃskṛtam .
dīyatāṃ me kṣudhārtāya tvāmuddiśyāgatāya ca .. 38.11 ..
38.d:
यवगोधूमशालीनामन्नं चैव सुसंस्कृतम् ।
दीयतां मे क्षुधार्ताय त्वामुद्दिश्यागताय च ॥ 38.11 ॥
38.m: "Let well-prepared food of barley, wheat, and rice / be given to me, who am distressed by hunger and have come on your account!"

38.s:
ityuktena tvasau vyādhaścintāṃ paramikāṃ gataḥ .
kva saṃbhaviṣyate mahyamiti cintāparo'bhavat .. 38.12 ..
38.d:
इत्युक्तेन त्वसौ व्याधश्चिन्तां परमिकां गतः ।
क्व संभविष्यते मह्यमिति चिन्तापरोऽभवत् ॥ 38.12 ॥
38.m: Addressed thus, that hunter fell into deep anxiety. / "Where will this come to be for me?"—thus he became absorbed in thought.

38.s:
tasya cintayataḥ pātramākāśāt patitaṃ śubham .
sauvarṇaṃ siddhisaṃyuktaṃ tajjagrāha kareṇa saḥ .. 38.13 ..
38.d:
तस्य चिन्तयतः पात्रमाकाशात् पतितं शुभम् ।
सौवर्णं सिद्धिसंयुक्तं तज्जग्राह करेण सः ॥ 38.13 ॥
38.m: As he was thinking, an auspicious golden vessel, / endowed with supernatural power, fell from the sky; he caught it with his hand.

38.s:
tad gṛhītvā muniṃ prāha durvāsākhyaṃ sasādhvasaḥ .
atraiva sthīyatāṃ brahman yāvad bhikṣāṭanaṃ tvaham .
karomi tatprasādo'yaṃ kriyatāṃ brahmavittama .. 38.14 ..
38.d:
तद् गृहीत्वा मुनिं प्राह दुर्वासाख्यं ससाध्वसः ।
अत्रैव स्थीयतां ब्रह्मन् यावद् भिक्षाटनं त्वहम् ।
करोमि तत्प्रसादोऽयं क्रियतां ब्रह्मवित्तम ॥ 38.14 ॥
38.m:
Taking it, he spoke with trepidation to the sage named Durvāsas:
“Remain right here, O holy one, while I wander for alms.
Best of knowers of the Brahman, grant this favor!”

38.s:
evamuktvā tato bhikṣāmaṭanaṃ vyādhasattamaḥ .
nātidūreṇa nagaraṃ dhanayoṣasamanvitam .. 38.15 ..
38.d:
एवमुक्त्वा ततो भिक्षामटनं व्याधसत्तमः ।
नातिदूरेण नगरं धनयोषसमन्वितम् ॥ 38.15 ॥
38.m:
Having spoken thus, that best of hunters then went wandering for alms
to a city not far away, filled with wealth and grain.

38.s:
tasya tatra prayātasya agrataḥ sarvaśobhanāḥ .
vṛkṣebhyo niryayuścānyā hemapātrāgrapāṇayaḥ .
vividhānnāni tasyāśu dattvā pātraṃ prapūritam .. 38.16 ..
38.d:
तस्य तत्र प्रयातस्य अग्रतः सर्वशोभनाः ।
वृक्षेभ्यो निर्ययुश्चान्या हेमपात्राग्रपाणयः ।
विविधान्नानि तस्याशु दत्त्वा पात्रं प्रपूरितम् ॥ 38.16 ॥

38.s:
sa ca bhūtārthamātmānaṃ matvā punarathāśramam .
ājagāma tato'paśyat tamṛṣiṃ japatāṃ varam .. 38.17 ..
38.d:
स च भूतार्थमात्मानं मत्वा पुनरथाश्रमम् ।
आजगाम ततोऽपश्यत् तमृषिं जपतां वरम् ॥ 38.17 ॥
38.m:
Considering his purpose achieved, he returned to the hermitage;
then he saw that sage, the best of those who chant [sacred prayers].

38.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā sthāpya tāṃ bhikṣāṃ śucau deśe prasannadhīḥ .
praṇamya tamṛṣiṃ vākyamuvāca vyādhasattamaḥ .. 38.18 ..
38.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा स्थाप्य तां भिक्षां शुचौ देशे प्रसन्नधीः ।
प्रणम्य तमृषिं वाक्यमुवाच व्याधसत्तमः ॥ 38.18 ॥
38.m:
Seeing him, he placed that almsfood in a pure spot; with a serene mind,
bowing down to that sage, the best of hunters spoke these words:

38.s:
bhagavan kṣālanaṃ padbhyāṃ kriyatāmṛṣipuṃgava .
yadi tvahamanugrāhyastadevaṃ karttumarhasi .. 38.19 ..
38.d:
भगवन् क्षालनं पद्भ्यां क्रियतामृषिपुंगव ।
यदि त्वहमनुग्राह्यस्तदेवं कर्त्तुमर्हसि ॥ 38.19 ॥
38.m:
“O Lord, let your feet be washed, O bull among sages.
If I am to receive your grace, you ought to do this.”

38.s:
evamuktaḥ sa jijñāsustapovīryaṃ śubhaṃ muniḥ .
nadīṃ gantuṃ na śaknomi jalapātraṃ na cāsti me .. 38.20 ..
38.d:
एवमुक्तः स जिज्ञासुस्तपोवीर्यं शुभं मुनिः ।
नदीं गन्तुं न शक्नोमि जलपात्रं न चास्ति मे ॥ 38.20 ॥
38.m:
Thus addressed, the sage, wishing to test the auspicious power of his asceticism, [said]:
“I am unable to go to the river, and I have no waterpot.

38.s:
kathaṃ prakṣālayāmyāśu vyādha pādau mahāmate .
ityetanmuninā vyādhaḥ śrutvā cintāparo'bhavat .
kiṃ karomi kathaṃ cāsya bhojanaṃ vai bhaviṣyati .. 38.21 ..
38.d:
कथं प्रक्षालयाम्याशु व्याध पादौ महामते ।
इत्येतन्मुनिना व्याधः श्रुत्वा चिन्तापरोऽभवत् ।
किं करोमि कथं चास्य भोजनं वै भविष्यति ॥ 38.21 ॥
38.m:
How, O wise hunter, am I quickly to wash my feet?”
Hearing this from the sage, the hunter became consumed with worry:
“What shall I do, and how indeed will his meal take place?”

38.s:
evaṃ saṃcintya manasā guruṃ smṛtvā vicakṣaṇaḥ .
jagāma śaraṇaṃ tāṃ tu saritaṃ devikāṃ sudhīḥ .. 38.22 ..
38.d:
एवं संचिन्त्य मनसा गुरुं स्मृत्वा विचक्षणः ।
जगाम शरणं तां तु सरितं देविकां सुधीः ॥ 38.22 ॥
38.m:
Pondering thus in his mind and remembering his guru, the discerning one,
wise in mind, took refuge in that river Devikā:

38.s:
vyādha uvāca .
vyādho'smi pāpakarmā'smi brahmahā'smi saridvare .
tathāpi saṃsmṛtā devi pāhi māṃ śaraṇaṃ gatam .. 38.23 ..
38.d:
व्याध उवाच ।
व्याधोऽस्मि पापकर्माऽस्मि ब्रह्महाऽस्मि सरिद्वरे ।
तथापि संस्मृता देवि पाहि मां शरणं गतम् ॥ 38.23 ॥
38.m:
The hunter said:
“A hunter am I, an evil-doer am I, a slayer of a brahmin am I, O best of rivers!
Yet, being remembered, O goddess, protect me who have come for refuge!

38.s:
devatāṃ naiva jānāmi na mantraṃ na tathārcanam .
gurupādau paraṃ dhyātvā paśyāmi satataṃ śubhe .. 38.24 ..
38.d:
देवतां नैव जानामि न मन्त्रं न तथार्चनम् ।
गुरुपादौ परं ध्यात्वा पश्यामि सततं शुभे ॥ 38.24 ॥
38.m:
I know neither deity, nor mantra, nor worship as such;
meditating only on my guru’s feet, O auspicious one, I behold [them] constantly.

38.s:
evaṃ vidhasya me devi dayāṃ kuru saridvare .
ṛṣeḥ kṣālārthasalilaṃ samīpaṃ kuru māciram .. 38.25 ..
38.d:
एवं विधस्य मे देवि दयां कुरु सरिद्वरे ।
ऋषेः क्षालार्थसलिलं समीपं कुरु माचिरम् ॥ 38.25 ॥
38.m:
Show mercy to one such as me, O goddess, best of rivers!
Bring water near for the sage’s washing without delay!”

38.s:
evamuktvā'tha vyādhena devikā pāpanāśinī .
ājagāma yatastasthau durvāsāḥ saṃśitavrataḥ .. 38.26 ..
38.d:
एवमुक्त्वाऽथ व्याधेन देविका पापनाशिनी ।
आजगाम यतस्तस्थौ दुर्वासाः संशितव्रतः ॥ 38.26 ॥
38.m:
When addressed thus by the hunter, the Devikā, destroyer of sins,
came to where Durvāsas of strict vows was staying.

38.s:
tasya pādau svayaṃ devī kṣālayantī saridvarā .
jagāma hrādinī bhūtvā vyādhāśramasamīpataḥ .. 38.27 ..
38.d:
तस्य पादौ स्वयं देवी क्षालयन्ती सरिद्वरा ।
जगाम ह्रादिनी भूत्वा व्याधाश्रमसमीपतः ॥ 38.27 ॥
38.m:
Herself washing his feet, that goddess, best of rivers,
became a roaring stream and flowed near the hunter’s hermitage.

38.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā mahadāścaryaṃ durvasā vismayaṃ yayau .
prakṣālya hastau pādau ca tadantaṃ śraddhayānvitam .
bubhuje paramaprītastathācamya vicakṣaṇaḥ .. 38.28 ..
38.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा महदाश्चर्यं दुर्वसा विस्मयं ययौ ।
प्रक्षाल्य हस्तौ पादौ च तदन्तं श्रद्धयान्वितम् ।
बुभुजे परमप्रीतस्तथाचम्य विचक्षणः ॥ 38.28 ॥
38.m:
Seeing that great wonder, Durvāsas was filled with astonishment.
Having washed his hands and feet, filled with faith, the wise one
ate that food with supreme delight and sipped water.

38.s:
tamasthiśeṣaṃ vyādhaṃ tu kṣudhādurbalatāṃ gatam .
uvāca vedādhyayanaṃ sarve vedāḥ sasaṃgrahāḥ .
brahmavidyā purāṇāni pratyakṣāṇi bhavantu te .. 38.29 ..
38.d:
तमस्थिशेषं व्याधं तु क्षुधादुर्बलतां गतम् ।
उवाच वेदाध्ययनं सर्वे वेदाः ससंग्रहाः ।
ब्रह्मविद्या पुराणानि प्रत्यक्षाणि भवन्तु ते ॥ 38.29 ॥
38.m:
To that hunter, who was reduced to mere bones and weakened by hunger,
he said: “Let the recitation of the Veda, all the Vedas along with their compendia,
the knowledge of the Brahman, and the Purāṇas become manifest before your eyes!”

38.s:
evaṃ prādād varaṃ tasya durvāsā nāma cākarot .
bhavān satyatapā nāma ṛṣirādyo bhaviṣyati .. 38.30 ..
38.d:
एवं प्रादाद् वरं तस्य दुर्वासा नाम चाकरोत् ।
भवान् सत्यतपा नाम ऋषिराद्यो भविष्यति ॥ 38.30 ॥
38.m:
Thus Durvāsas granted him a boon and gave him a name:
“You shall become the foremost sage named Satyatapas.”

38.s:
evaṃ dattavaro vyādhastamāha munisattamam .
vyādho bhūtvā kathaṃ brahman vedānadhyāpayāmyaham .. 38.31 ..
38.d:
एवं दत्तवरो व्याधस्तमाह मुनिसत्तमम् ।
व्याधो भूत्वा कथं ब्रह्मन् वेदानध्यापयाम्यहम् ॥ 38.31 ॥
38.m:
Having been granted the boon in this way, the hunter said to that best of sages:
“Being a hunter, how, O holy one, shall I teach the Vedas?”

38.s:
ṛṣiruvāca .
prākśarīraṃ gataṃ te'dya nirāhārasya sattama .
tapomayaṃ śarīraṃ te pṛthagbhūtaṃ na saṃśayaḥ .. 38.32 ..
38.d:
ऋषिरुवाच ।
प्राक्शरीरं गतं तेऽद्य निराहारस्य सत्तम ।
तपोमयं शरीरं ते पृथग्भूतं न संशयः ॥ 38.32 ॥

38.s:
prāgvijñānaṃ gataṃ nāśamidānīṃ śuddhamakṣaram .
viddhi taṃ śuddhakāyo'si tathā'nyat te śarīrakam .
tena vedāḥ samaṃ śāstraiḥ pratibhāsyanti te mune .. 38.33 ..
38.d:
प्राग्विज्ञानं गतं नाशमिदानीं शुद्धमक्षरम् ।
विद्धि तं शुद्धकायोऽसि तथाऽन्यत् ते शरीरकम् ।
तेन वेदाः समं शास्त्रैः प्रतिभास्यन्ति ते मुने ॥ 38.33 ॥

38.s: .. iti śrīvarāhapurāṇe bhagavacchāstre aṣṭatriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 38 ..
38.d: ॥ इति श्रीवराहपुराणे भगवच्छास्त्रे अष्टत्रिंशोऽध्यायः ॥ 38 ॥
38.m: Thus ends the thirty-eighth chapter in the venerable Varāha Purāṇa, a scripture of the Lord.

39.s:
satyatapā uvāca .
bhagavan dve śarīre tu iti yatparikīrttitam .
tanme kathaya bhedaṃ vai ke te brahmavidāṃ vara .. 39.1 ..
39.d:
सत्यतपा उवाच ।
भगवन् द्वे शरीरे तु इति यत्परिकीर्त्तितम् ।
तन्मे कथय भेदं वै के ते ब्रह्मविदां वर ॥ 39.1 ॥
39.m:
Satyatapas said:
“O Lord, regarding the two bodies that were spoken of:
tell me their distinction, what are they, O best of the knowers of the Brahman?”

39.s:
durvāsā uvāca .
na dve trīṇi śarīrāṇi vācyaṃ tadviparītakam .
vibhogāyatanaṃ caiva triśarīrāṇi prāṇinām .. 39.2 ..
39.d:
दुर्वासा उवाच ।
न द्वे त्रीणि शरीराणि वाच्यं तद्विपरीतकम् ।
विभोगायतनं चैव त्रिशरीराणि प्राणिनाम् ॥ 39.2 ॥

39.s:
prāgavasthamadharmākhyaṃ parijñānavivarjitam .
aparaṃ savrataṃ taddhi jñeyamatyantadhārmikam .. 39.3 ..
39.d:
प्रागवस्थमधर्माख्यं परिज्ञानविवर्जितम् ।
अपरं सव्रतं तद्धि ज्ञेयमत्यन्तधार्मिकम् ॥ 39.3 ॥
39.m:
The former state is termed unrighteousness, devoid of thorough understanding;
the other is endowed with vows, to be known as exceedingly righteous.

39.s:
dharmādharmopabhogāya yat tṛtīyamatīndriyam .
tattribhedaṃ vinirdiṣṭaṃ brahmavidbhirvicakṣaṇaiḥ .
yātanā dharmabhogaśca bhuktiśceti tribhedakam .. 39.4 ..
39.d:
धर्माधर्मोपभोगाय यत् तृतीयमतीन्द्रियम् ।
तत्त्रिभेदं विनिर्दिष्टं ब्रह्मविद्भिर्विचक्षणैः ।
यातना धर्मभोगश्च भुक्तिश्चेति त्रिभेदकम् ॥ 39.4 ॥

39.s:
yastu bhāvaḥ purā hyāsīt prāṇino nighnataḥ sa vai .
tatpāpākhyaṃ śarīraṃ te pāpasaṃjñaṃ taducyate .. 39.5 ..
39.d:
यस्तु भावः पुरा ह्यासीत् प्राणिनो निघ्नतः स वै ।
तत्पापाख्यं शरीरं ते पापसंज्ञं तदुच्यते ॥ 39.5 ॥
39.m:
That disposition which you formerly had when slaying living creatures,
that is called your sinful body; it is designated as sinful.

39.s:
idānīṃ śubhavṛttiṃ tu kurvatastapa ārjavam .
aparaṃ dharmarūpaṃ tu śarīraṃ te vyavasthitam .
tena vedapurāṇāni jñātumarhasyasaṃśayam .. 39.6 ..
39.d:
इदानीं शुभवृत्तिं तु कुर्वतस्तप आर्जवम् ।
अपरं धर्मरूपं तु शरीरं ते व्यवस्थितम् ।
तेन वेदपुराणानि ज्ञातुमर्हस्यसंशयम् ॥ 39.6 ॥

39.s:
yadāṣṭākaṃ saṃparivarttate pumāṃ-
stadā tryavasthaḥ parikīrtyate tu vai .
gatāṣṭavargastrigataḥ sadā śubhaḥ
sthiro bhavedātmani niścayātmavān .. 39.7 ..
39.d:
यदाष्टाकं संपरिवर्त्तते पुमां-
स्तदा त्र्यवस्थः परिकीर्त्यते तु वै ।
गताष्टवर्गस्त्रिगतः सदा शुभः
स्थिरो भवेदात्मनि निश्चयात्मवान् ॥ 39.7 ॥
39.m:
When a man revolves in the eightfold [aggregate],
then indeed he is proclaimed to be of three states;
freed from the eightfold group, gone beyond the three, ever auspicious,
resolute in nature, he becomes established in the Self.

39.s:
yadā pañca punaḥ pañca pañca pañcāpi saṃtyajet .
ekamārgastadā brahma śāśvataṃ labhate naraḥ .. 39.8 ..
39.d:
यदा पञ्च पुनः पञ्च पञ्च पञ्चापि संत्यजेत् ।
एकमार्गस्तदा ब्रह्म शाश्वतं लभते नरः ॥ 39.8 ॥
39.m:
When he casts off five, and five, and five, and also five,
then a man, walking the single path, attains the eternal Brahman.”

39.s:
satyatapā uvāca .
bhagavan yadi vijñānaṃ śarīraṃ nopajāyate .
tadā kena prakāreṇa paraṃ brahmopalabhyate .. 39.9 ..
39.d:
सत्यतपा उवाच ।
भगवन् यदि विज्ञानं शरीरं नोपजायते ।
तदा केन प्रकारेण परं ब्रह्मोपलभ्यते ॥ 39.9 ॥
39.m:
Satyatapas said:
“O Lord, if a body of understanding does not arise,
then by what means is the supreme Brahman attained?”

39.s:
durvāsā uvāca .
karmakāṇḍaṃ jñānamūlaṃ jñānaṃ karmādikaṃ tathā .
etayorantaraṃ nāsti yathā'śmamṛdayormune .. 39.10 ..
39.d:
दुर्वासा उवाच ।
कर्मकाण्डं ज्ञानमूलं ज्ञानं कर्मादिकं तथा ।
एतयोरन्तरं नास्ति यथाऽश्ममृदयोर्मुने ॥ 39.10 ॥

39.s:
karmakāṇḍaṃ caturbhedaṃ brāhmaṇādiṣu kīrtitam .
tatra vedoktakarmāṇi trayaḥ kurvanti nityaśaḥ .
triśuśrūṣāmathaikastu eṣā vedoditā kriyā .. 39.11 ..
39.d:
कर्मकाण्डं चतुर्भेदं ब्राह्मणादिषु कीर्तितम् ।
तत्र वेदोक्तकर्माणि त्रयः कुर्वन्ति नित्यशः ।
त्रिशुश्रूषामथैकस्तु एषा वेदोदिता क्रिया ॥ 39.11 ॥

39.s:
etān dharmānavasthāya brahmaṇopāstiṃ rocate .
tasya muktirbhavennūnaṃ vedavādaratasya ca .. 39.12 ..
39.d:
एतान् धर्मानवस्थाय ब्रह्मणोपास्तिं रोचते ।
तस्य मुक्तिर्भवेन्नूनं वेदवादरतस्य च ॥ 39.12 ॥
39.m:
For one who, abiding by these duties, finds delight in the contemplation of the Brahman
and is devoted to the teachings of the Veda, liberation will surely arise.”

39.s:
satyatapā uvāca .
yadetat paramaṃ brahma tvayā proktaṃ mahāmune .
tasya rūpaṃ na jānanti yogino'pi mahātmanaḥ .. 39.13 ..
39.d:
सत्यतपा उवाच ।
यदेतत् परमं ब्रह्म त्वया प्रोक्तं महामुने ।
तस्य रूपं न जानन्ति योगिनोऽपि महात्मनः ॥ 39.13 ॥
39.m:
Satyatapas said:
“This supreme Brahman that has been spoken of by you, O great sage—
even great-souled yogins do not know its form.

39.s:
anāmamasagotraṃ ca amūrttaṃ mūrttivarjitam .
kathaṃ sa jñāyate brahma saṃjñānāmavivarjitam .
tasya saṃjñāṃ kathaya me vedamārgavyavasthitām .. 39.14 ..
39.d:
अनाममसगोत्रं च अमूर्त्तं मूर्त्तिवर्जितम् ।
कथं स ज्ञायते ब्रह्म संज्ञानामविवर्जितम् ।
तस्य संज्ञां कथय मे वेदमार्गव्यवस्थिताम् ॥ 39.14 ॥
39.m:
Nameless, without lineage, formless, devoid of shape—
how is that Brahman, free of designation and name, to be known?
Tell me its designation as established on the path of the Veda.”

39.s:
durvāsā uvāca .
yadetat paramaṃ brahma vedavyāseṣu paṭhyate .
sa devaḥ puṇḍarīkākṣaḥ svayaṃ nārāyaṇaḥ paraḥ .. 39.15 ..
39.d:
दुर्वासा उवाच ।
यदेतत् परमं ब्रह्म वेदव्यासेषु पठ्यते ।
स देवः पुण्डरीकाक्षः स्वयं नारायणः परः ॥ 39.15 ॥
39.m:
Durvāsas said:
“This supreme Brahman that is recited in the compilations of the Vedas
is that lotus-eyed god himself, the supreme Nārāyaṇa.

39.s:
sa yajñairvividhairiṣṭairdānairdattaiśca sattama .
prāpyate paramo devaḥ svayaṃ nārāyaṇo hariḥ .. 39.16 ..
39.d:
स यज्ञैर्विविधैरिष्टैर्दानैर्दत्तैश्च सत्तम ।
प्राप्यते परमो देवः स्वयं नारायणो हरिः ॥ 39.16 ॥
39.m:
He is attained through various sacrifices offered, and gifts bestowed, O best of men:
the supreme God, Hari, Nārāyaṇa himself.”

39.s:
satyatapā uvāca .
bhagavan bahuvittena ṛtvigbhirvedapāragaiḥ .
prāpyate puṇyakṛdbhirhi kvacid yajñaḥ kathaṃcana .
tena prāptena bhagavān labhyate duḥkhato hariḥ .. 39.17 ..
39.d:
सत्यतपा उवाच ।
भगवन् बहुवित्तेन ऋत्विग्भिर्वेदपारगैः ।
प्राप्यते पुण्यकृद्भिर्हि क्वचिद् यज्ञः कथंचन ।
तेन प्राप्तेन भगवान् लभ्यते दुःखतो हरिः ॥ 39.17 ॥
39.m: Satyatapas said: / O Lord, only with vast wealth and priests who have mastered the Vedas / is a sacrifice ever attained, somehow, by doers of merit. / Even when it is attained, the Lord Hari is reached [only] with difficulty.

39.s:
vittena ca vinā dānaṃ dātuṃ vipra na śakyate .
vidyamāne'pi na matiḥ kuṭumbāsaktacetasaḥ .
tasya mokṣaḥ kathaṃ brahman sarvathā durlabho hariḥ .. 39.18 ..
39.d:
वित्तेन च विना दानं दातुं विप्र न शक्यते ।
विद्यमानेऽपि न मतिः कुटुम्बासक्तचेतसः ।
तस्य मोक्षः कथं ब्रह्मन् सर्वथा दुर्लभो हरिः ॥ 39.18 ॥
39.m: And without wealth, O brāhmaṇa, one cannot give gifts. / Even when wealth is present, the mind of one attached to family does not turn [to it]. / How can there be liberation for such a person, O Brahmā? Hari is utterly difficult to attain.

39.s:
alpāyāsena labhyeta yena devaḥ sanātanaḥ .
tanme sāmānyato brūhi sarvavarṇeṣu yad bhavet .. 39.19 ..
39.d:
अल्पायासेन लभ्येत येन देवः सनातनः ।
तन्मे सामान्यतो ब्रूहि सर्ववर्णेषु यद् भवेत् ॥ 39.19 ॥
39.m: Tell me, in general terms, that by which the eternal God / may be attained with little exertion, and which is open to all social classes.

39.s:
durvāsā uvāca .
kathayāmi paraṃ guhyaṃ rahasyaṃ devanirmitam .
dharaṇyā yatkṛtaṃ pūrvaṃ majjantyā tu rasātale .. 39.20 ..
39.d:
दुर्वासा उवाच ।
कथयामि परं गुह्यं रहस्यं देवनिर्मितम् ।
धरण्या यत्कृतं पूर्वं मज्जन्त्या तु रसातले ॥ 39.20 ॥
39.m: Durvāsas said: / I will tell you the supreme secret, the mystery ordained by the gods, / which was performed of old by Dharaṇī as she was sinking into Rasātala.

39.s:
pṛthivyāḥ pārthivo bhāvaḥ salile nātirecitaḥ .
tasmin salilamagne tu pṛthvī prāyād rasātalam .. 39.21 ..
39.d:
पृथिव्याः पार्थिवो भावः सलिले नातिरेचितः ।
तस्मिन् सलिलमग्ने तु पृथ्वी प्रायाद् रसातलम् ॥ 39.21 ॥
39.m: The earthy nature of the Earth was not overwhelmed in the water. / But when that [earthly realm] was submerged in the water, the Earth sank down to Rasātala.

39.s:
sā bhūtadhāriṇī devī rasātalagatā śubhā .
ārādhayāmāsa vibhuṃ devaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ param .
upavāsavratairdevī niyamaiśca pṛthagvidhaiḥ .. 39.22 ..
39.d:
सा भूतधारिणी देवी रसातलगता शुभा ।
आराधयामास विभुं देवं नारायणं परम् ।
उपवासव्रतैर्देवी नियमैश्च पृथग्विधैः ॥ 39.22 ॥
39.m: Gone down to Rasātala, that auspicious goddess, bearer of all beings, / propitiated the all-pervading supreme God Nārāyaṇa / with fasting observances, the goddess, and various kinds of disciplines.

39.s:
kālena mahatā tasyāḥ prasanno garuḍadhvajaḥ .
ujjahāra sthitau cemāṃ sthāpayāmāsa so'vyayaḥ .. 39.23 ..
39.d:
कालेन महता तस्याः प्रसन्नो गरुडध्वजः ।
उज्जहार स्थितौ चेमां स्थापयामास सोऽव्ययः ॥ 39.23 ॥
39.m: After a long time, the Garuḍa-bannered [Lord] was pleased with her; / the imperishable one lifted her up and established her in stability.

39.s:
satyatapā uvāca .
ko'sau dharaṇyā saṃcīrṇa upavāso mahāmune .
kāni vratāni ca tathā etanme vaktumarhasi .. 39.24 ..
39.d:
सत्यतपा उवाच ।
कोऽसौ धरण्या संचीर्ण उपवासो महामुने ।
कानि व्रतानि च तथा एतन्मे वक्तुमर्हसि ॥ 39.24 ॥
39.m: Satyatapas said: / What was that fast undertaken by Dharaṇī, O great sage, / and what were the observances? Please tell me this.

39.s:
durvāsā uvāca .
yadā mārgaśire māsi daśamyāṃ niyatātmavān .
kṛtvā devārcanaṃ dhīmānagnikāryaṃ yathāvidhi .. 39.25 ..
39.d:
दुर्वासा उवाच ।
यदा मार्गशिरे मासि दशम्यां नियतात्मवान् ।
कृत्वा देवार्चनं धीमानग्निकार्यं यथाविधि ॥ 39.25 ॥
39.m: Durvāsas said: / When, in the month of Mārgaśīrṣa, on the tenth day, the self-controlled, / wise person has performed worship of the deity and the fire ritual according to rule,

39.s:
śucivāsāḥ prasannātmā havyamannaṃ susaṃskṛtam .
bhuktvā pañcapadaṃ gatvā punaḥ śaucaṃ tu pādayoḥ .. 39.26 ..
39.d:
शुचिवासाः प्रसन्नात्मा हव्यमन्नं सुसंस्कृतम् ।
भुक्त्वा पञ्चपदं गत्वा पुनः शौचं तु पादयोः ॥ 39.26 ॥
39.m: wearing clean garments, joyful in mind, having eaten / sacrificial food that is well prepared, having walked five steps and again washed his feet,

39.s:
kṛtvā'ṣṭāṅgulamātraṃ tu kṣīravṛkṣasamudbhavam .
bhakṣayed dantakāṣṭhaṃ tu tata ācamya yatnataḥ .. 39.27 ..
39.d:
कृत्वाऽष्टाङ्गुलमात्रं तु क्षीरवृक्षसमुद्भवम् ।
भक्षयेद् दन्तकाष्ठं तु तत आचम्य यत्नतः ॥ 39.27 ॥
39.m: and having used a tooth-stick measuring eight finger-breadths / obtained from a milky-sap tree, he should then carefully sip water;

39.s:
spṛṣṭvā dvārāṇi sarvāṇi ciraṃ dhyātvā janārdanam .
śaṅkhacakragadāpāṇiṃ kirīṭiṃ pītavāsasam .. 39.28 ..
39.d:
स्पृष्ट्वा द्वाराणि सर्वाणि चिरं ध्यात्वा जनार्दनम् ।
शङ्खचक्रगदापाणिं किरीटिं पीतवाससम् ॥ 39.28 ॥
39.m: having touched all the bodily apertures and meditated for a long time on Janārdana, / who holds the conch, discus, and mace in his hands, wears a diadem and yellow robes,

39.s:
prasannavadanaṃ devaṃ sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitam .
dhyātvā punarjalaṃ haste gṛhya bhānuṃ janārdanam .. 39.29 ..
39.d:
प्रसन्नवदनं देवं सर्वलक्षणलक्षितम् ।
ध्यात्वा पुनर्जलं हस्ते गृह्य भानुं जनार्दनम् ॥ 39.29 ॥
39.m: the smiling-faced God endowed with all auspicious marks— / having meditated, taking water in his hand, [contemplating] Janārdana as the sun,

39.s:
dhyātvā'rdhyaṃ dāpayet tasya karatoyena mānavaḥ .
evamuccārayed vācaṃ tasmin kāle mahāmune .. 39.30 ..
39.d:
ध्यात्वाऽर्ध्यं दापयेत् तस्य करतोयेन मानवः ।
एवमुच्चारयेद् वाचं तस्मिन् काले महामुने ॥ 39.30 ॥
39.m: a man should offer water-oblation to him with the water from his hands. / At that time, O great sage, he should utter these words:

39.s:
ekādaśyāṃ nirāhāraḥ sthitvā'hamapare'hani .
bhokṣyāmi puṇḍarīkākṣa śaraṇaṃ me bhavācyuta .. 39.31 ..
39.d:
एकादश्यां निराहारः स्थित्वाऽहमपरेऽहनि ।
भोक्ष्यामि पुण्डरीकाक्ष शरणं मे भवाच्युत ॥ 39.31 ॥
39.m: ‘Remaining without food on the eleventh, I will eat on the next day, / O lotus-eyed one; be my refuge, O Acyuta!’

39.s:
evamuktvā tato rātrau devadevasya sannidhau .
japannārāyaṇāyeti svapet tatra vidhānataḥ .. 39.32 ..
39.d:
एवमुक्त्वा ततो रात्रौ देवदेवस्य सन्निधौ ।
जपन्नारायणायेति स्वपेत् तत्र विधानतः ॥ 39.32 ॥
39.m: Having spoken thus, he should then sleep according to rule at night / near the God of gods, reciting, ‘To Nārāyaṇa.’

39.s:
tataḥ prabhāte vimale nadīṃ gatvā samudragām .
itarāṃ vā taḍāgaṃ vā gṛhe vā niyatātmavān .. 39.33 ..
39.d:
ततः प्रभाते विमले नदीं गत्वा समुद्रगाम् ।
इतरां वा तडागं वा गृहे वा नियतात्मवान् ॥ 39.33 ॥
39.m: Then, at pure dawn, having gone to an ocean-going river / or another [stream], or to a pond, or remaining self-controlled at home,

39.s:
ānīya mṛttikāṃ śuddhāṃ mantreṇānena mānavaḥ .
dhāraṇaṃ poṣaṇaṃ tvatto bhūtānāṃ devi sarvadā .
tena satyena me pāpaṃ yāvanmocaya suvrate .. 39.34 ..
39.d:
आनीय मृत्तिकां शुद्धां मन्त्रेणानेन मानवः ।
धारणं पोषणं त्वत्तो भूतानां देवि सर्वदा ।
तेन सत्येन मे पापं यावन्मोचय सुव्रते ॥ 39.34 ॥
39.m: having brought clean earth, a man [recites] with this mantra: / ‘From you, O goddess, comes the perpetual bearing and nourishment of creatures; / by that truth, O faithful one, release my sin as far as it extends!

39.s:
brahmāṇḍodaratīrthāni karaiḥ spṛṣṭāni deva te .
tenemāṃ mṛttikāṃ spṛṣṭvā mā labhāmi tvayoditām .. 39.35 ..
39.d:
ब्रह्माण्डोदरतीर्थानि करैः स्पृष्टानि देव ते ।
तेनेमां मृत्तिकां स्पृष्ट्वा मा लभामि त्वयोदिताम् ॥ 39.35 ॥
39.m: The sacred waters within the womb of the cosmic egg have been touched by your rays, O God; / having touched this earth by that, may I not incur what has been censured by you.

39.s:
tvayi sarve rasā nityāḥ sthitā varuṇa sarvadā .
tenemāṃ mṛttikāṃ plāvya pūtāṃ kuru mamāciram .. 39.36 ..
39.d:
त्वयि सर्वे रसा नित्याः स्थिता वरुण सर्वदा ।
तेनेमां मृत्तिकां प्लाव्य पूतां कुरु ममाचिरम् ॥ 39.36 ॥
39.m: All essences, O Varuṇa, always abide in you; / therefore, inundating this earth, make it pure for me without delay.’

39.s:
evaṃ mṛdaṃ tathā toyaṃ prasādyātmānamālabhet .
triḥ kṛtvā śeṣamṛdayā kuṇḍamālikhya vai jale .. 39.37 ..
39.d:
एवं मृदं तथा तोयं प्रसाद्यात्मानमालभेत् ।
त्रिः कृत्वा शेषमृदया कुण्डमालिख्य वै जले ॥ 39.37 ॥
39.m: Having thus propitiated the earth and the water, he should touch himself / three times with the remaining earth, having traced an enclosure in the water.

39.s:
tatastatra naraḥ samyak cakravartyupacārataḥ .
snātvā cāvaśyakaṃ kṛtvā punardevagṛhaṃ vrajet .. 39.38 ..
39.d:
ततस्तत्र नरः सम्यक् चक्रवर्त्युपचारतः ।
स्नात्वा चावश्यकं कृत्वा पुनर्देवगृहं व्रजेत् ॥ 39.38 ॥
39.m: Then, having properly bathed there with the royal attendance of an emperor / and having performed the obligatory rites, a man should return to the deity’s shrine.

39.s:
tatrārādhya mahāyogiṃ devaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ prabhum .
keśavāya namaḥ pādau kaṭiṃ dāmodarāya ca .. 39.39 ..
39.d:
तत्राराध्य महायोगिं देवं नारायणं प्रभुम् ।
केशवाय नमः पादौ कटिं दामोदराय च ॥ 39.39 ॥
39.m: There, having worshipped the great yogin, the Lord God Nārāyaṇa: / ‘Obeisance to Keśava,’ the two feet; and the waist to Dāmodara;

39.s:
ūruyugmaṃ nṛsiṃhāya uraḥ śrīvatsadhāriṇe .
kaṇṭhaṃ kaustubhanāthāya vakṣaḥ śrīpataye tathā .. 39.40 ..
39.d:
ऊरुयुग्मं नृसिंहाय उरः श्रीवत्सधारिणे ।
कण्ठं कौस्तुभनाथाय वक्षः श्रीपतये तथा ॥ 39.40 ॥
39.m: the two thighs to Nṛsiṃha; the chest to the bearer of the Śrīvatsa; / the throat to the Lord of the Kaustubha; and the breast to the Lord of Śrī;

39.s:
trailokyavijayāyeti bāhū sarvātmane śiraḥ .
rathāṅgadhāriṇe cakraṃ śaṃkarāyeti vārijam .. 39.41 ..
39.d:
त्रैलोक्यविजयायेति बाहू सर्वात्मने शिरः ।
रथाङ्गधारिणे चक्रं शंकरायेति वारिजम् ॥ 39.41 ॥
39.m: the arms with ‘To the conqueror of the three worlds’; the head with ‘To the Self of all’; / the discus to the wielder of the chariot-wheel; the conch with ‘To the bringer of auspiciousness’;

39.s:
gambhīrāyeti ca gadāmambhojaṃ śāntimūrttaye .
evamabhyarcya deveśaṃ devaṃ nārāyaṇaṃ prabhum .. 39.42 ..
39.d:
गम्भीरायेति च गदामम्भोजं शान्तिमूर्त्तये ।
एवमभ्यर्च्य देवेशं देवं नारायणं प्रभुम् ॥ 39.42 ॥
39.m: the mace with ‘To the profound one’; and the lotus with ‘To the embodiment of peace.’ / Having thus worshipped the Lord of gods, the supreme Lord Nārāyaṇa,

39.s:
punastasyāgrataḥ kumbhān caturaḥ sthāpayed budhaḥ .
jalapūrṇān samālyāṃśca sitacandanalepitān .. 39.43 ..
39.d:
पुनस्तस्याग्रतः कुम्भान् चतुरः स्थापयेद् बुधः ।
जलपूर्णान् समाल्यांश्च सितचन्दनलेपितान् ॥ 39.43 ॥
39.m: the wise man should then place four jars before him, / filled with water, adorned with garlands, and smeared with white sandalwood,

39.s:
cūtapallavasagrīvān sitavastrāvaguṇṭhitān .
sthagitān tāmrapātraiśca tilapūrṇaiḥ sakāñcanaiḥ .. 39.44 ..
39.d:
चूतपल्लवसग्रीवान् सितवस्त्रावगुण्ठितान् ।
स्थगितान् ताम्रपात्रैश्च तिलपूर्णैः सकाञ्चनैः ॥ 39.44 ॥
39.m: with necks covered with mango leaves, wrapped in white cloth, / and covered with copper vessels filled with sesame seeds and gold.

39.s:
catvāraste samudrāstu kalaśāḥ parikīrtitāḥ .
teṣāṃ madhye śubhaṃ pīṭhaṃ sthāpayed vastragarbhitam .. 39.45 ..
39.d:
चत्वारस्ते समुद्रास्तु कलशाः परिकीर्तिताः ।
तेषां मध्ये शुभं पीठं स्थापयेद् वस्त्रगर्भितम् ॥ 39.45 ॥
39.m: Those four pots are celebrated as the four oceans. / In their midst he should set up an auspicious seat lined with cloth.

39.s:
tasmin sauvarṇaraupyaṃ vā tāmraṃ vā dāravaṃ tathā .
alābhe sarvapātrāṇāṃ pālāśaṃ pātramiṣyate .. 39.46 ..
39.d:
तस्मिन् सौवर्णरौप्यं वा ताम्रं वा दारवं तथा ।
अलाभे सर्वपात्राणां पालाशं पात्रमिष्यते ॥ 39.46 ॥
39.m: On it [he should place a vessel] of gold, silver, copper, or wood; / if all these vessels are unavailable, a palāśa-wood vessel is prescribed.

39.s:
toyapūrṇaṃ tu tatkṛtvā tasmin pātre tato nyaset .
sauvarṇaṃ matsyrūpeṇa kṛtvā devaṃ janārdam .
vedavedāṅgasaṃyuktaṃ śrutismṛtivibhūṣitam .. 39.47 ..
39.d:
तोयपूर्णं तु तत्कृत्वा तस्मिन् पात्रे ततो न्यसेत् ।
सौवर्णं मत्स्य्रूपेण कृत्वा देवं जनार्दम् ।
वेदवेदाङ्गसंयुक्तं श्रुतिस्मृतिविभूषितम् ॥ 39.47 ॥
39.m: Having filled that vessel with water, he should then place in it / the God Janārdana made of gold in the form of a fish, / accompanied by the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, adorned with Śruti and Smṛti,

39.s:
tatrānekavidhairbhakṣaiḥ phalaiḥ puṣpaiśca śobhitam .
gandhadhūpaiśca vastraiśca arcayitvā yathāvidhi .. 39.48 ..
39.d:
तत्रानेकविधैर्भक्षैः फलैः पुष्पैश्च शोभितम् ।
गन्धधूपैश्च वस्त्रैश्च अर्चयित्वा यथाविधि ॥ 39.48 ॥
39.m: adorned with many kinds of eatables, fruits, and flowers, / having worshipped him according to rule with scents, incense, and clothes [saying]:

39.s:
rasātalagatā vedā yathā deva tvayāhṛtāḥ .
matsyarūpeṇa tadvanmāṃ bhavānuddhara keśava .
evamuccārya tasyāgre jāgaraṃ tatra kārayet .. 39.49 ..
39.d:
रसातलगता वेदा यथा देव त्वयाहृताः ।
मत्स्यरूपेण तद्वन्मां भवानुद्धर केशव ।
एवमुच्चार्य तस्याग्रे जागरं तत्र कारयेत् ॥ 39.49 ॥
39.m: ‘Just as the Vedas that had gone to Rasātala were retrieved by you, O God, / in the form of a fish, so do you deliver me, O Keśava!’ / Having uttered this before him, he should keep a vigil there.

39.s:
yathāvibhavasāreṇa prabhāte vimale tathā .
caturṇāṃ brāhmaṇānāṃ ca caturo dāpayed ghaṭān .. 39.50 ..
39.d:
यथाविभवसारेण प्रभाते विमले तथा ।
चतुर्णां ब्राह्मणानां च चतुरो दापयेद् घटान् ॥ 39.50 ॥
39.m: According to the extent of his wealth, at clear dawn, / he should give the four pots to four brāhmaṇas.

39.s:
pūrvaṃ tu bahvṛce dadyācchandoge dakṣiṇaṃ tathā .
yajuḥśākhānvite dadyāt paścimaṃ ghaṭamuttamam .
uttaraṃ kāmato tadyādeṣa eva vidhiḥ smṛtaḥ .. 39.51 ..
39.d:
पूर्वं तु बह्वृचे दद्याच्छन्दोगे दक्षिणं तथा ।
यजुःशाखान्विते दद्यात् पश्चिमं घटमुत्तमम् ।
उत्तरं कामतो तद्यादेष एव विधिः स्मृतः ॥ 39.51 ॥
39.m: He should give the eastern one to a Ṛgvedic priest, the southern one to a chanter of the Sāmaveda, / and the excellent western pot to one proficient in a branch of the Yajurveda; / he may give the northern one at will; this indeed is the recorded rule:

39.s:
ṛgvedaḥ prīyatāṃ pūrve sāmavedastu dakṣiṇe .
yajurvedaḥ paścimato atharvaścottareṇa tu .. 39.52 ..
39.d:
ऋग्वेदः प्रीयतां पूर्वे सामवेदस्तु दक्षिणे ।
यजुर्वेदः पश्चिमतो अथर्वश्चोत्तरेण तु ॥ 39.52 ॥
39.m: ‘May the Ṛgveda be pleased in the east, the Sāmaveda in the south, / the Yajurveda in the west, and the Atharvaveda in the north.’

39.s:
anena kramayogena prīyatāmiti vācayet .
matsyarūpaṃ ca sauvarṇamācāryāya nivedayet .. 39.53 ..
39.d:
अनेन क्रमयोगेन प्रीयतामिति वाचयेत् ।
मत्स्यरूपं च सौवर्णमाचार्याय निवेदयेत् ॥ 39.53 ॥
39.m: In this order, he should have them say: ‘May it be pleased!’ / And he should present the golden fish-form to the preceptor,

39.s:
gandhadhūpādivastraiśca saṃpūjya vidhivat kramāt .
yastvimaṃ sarahasyaṃ ca mantraṃ caivopapādayet .
vidhānaṃ tasya vai dattvā phalaṃ koṭiguṇottaram .. 39.54 ..
39.d:
गन्धधूपादिवस्त्रैश्च संपूज्य विधिवत् क्रमात् ।
यस्त्विमं सरहस्यं च मन्त्रं चैवोपपादयेत् ।
विधानं तस्य वै दत्त्वा फलं कोटिगुणोत्तरम् ॥ 39.54 ॥
39.m: having worshipped him in due order according to rule with scents, incense, clothes, and the like. / Whoever imparts this ritual along with its secret and its mantra, / having given [a gift] to him, receives a fruit ten million times greater.

39.s:
pratipadya guruṃ yastu mohād vipratipadyate .
sa janmakoṭi narake pacyate puruṣādhamaḥ .
vidhānasya pradātā yo gururityucyate budhaiḥ .. 39.55 ..
39.d:
प्रतिपद्य गुरुं यस्तु मोहाद् विप्रतिपद्यते ।
स जन्मकोटि नरके पच्यते पुरुषाधमः ।
विधानस्य प्रदाता यो गुरुरित्युच्यते बुधैः ॥ 39.55 ॥
39.m: He who, having accepted a guru, turns against him out of delusion, / that lowest of men is cooked in hell for ten million births. / The one who provides the ritual is called the guru by the wise.

39.s:
evaṃ dattvā vidhānena dvādaśyāṃ viṣṇumarcya ca .
viprāṇāṃ bhojanaṃ kuryād yathāśaktyā sadakṣiṇam .. 39.56 ..
39.d:
एवं दत्त्वा विधानेन द्वादश्यां विष्णुमर्च्य च ।
विप्राणां भोजनं कुर्याद् यथाशक्त्या सदक्षिणम् ॥ 39.56 ॥
39.m: Having given in this manner according to the rite, and having worshipped Viṣṇu on the twelfth lunar day, / he should feed brāhmaṇas according to his capacity, along with monetary gifts.

39.s:
tāmrapātraiśca satilaiḥ sthagitān kārayed ghaṭān .
tatra sajjalapātrasthaṃ brāhmaṇāya kuṭumbine .. 39.57 ..
39.d:
ताम्रपात्रैश्च सतिलैः स्थगितान् कारयेद् घटान् ।
तत्र सज्जलपात्रस्थं ब्राह्मणाय कुटुम्बिने ॥ 39.57 ॥
39.m: And he should cause jars to be covered with copper vessels containing sesame seeds. / There, [placing] the god upon a vessel filled with water, to a brāhmaṇa who is a householder,

39.s:
devaṃ dadyānmahābhāgastato viprāṃśca bhojayet .
bhūriṇā paramānnena tataḥ paścāt svayaṃ naraḥ .
bhuñjīta sahito bālairvāgyataḥ saṃyatendriyaḥ .. 39.58 ..
39.d:
देवं दद्यान्महाभागस्ततो विप्रांश्च भोजयेत् ।
भूरिणा परमान्नेन ततः पश्चात् स्वयं नरः ।
भुञ्जीत सहितो बालैर्वाग्यतः संयतेन्द्रियः ॥ 39.58 ॥
39.m: the fortunate man should give the god, and then feed the brāhmaṇas / with abundant milk-rice; after that, the man himself / should eat together with children, keeping silent with senses restrained.

39.s:
anena vidhinā yastu dharaṇīvratakṛnnaraḥ .
tasya puṇyaphalaṃ cāgryaṃ śrṛṇu buddhimatāṃ vara .. 39.59 ..
39.d:
अनेन विधिना यस्तु धरणीव्रतकृन्नरः ।
तस्य पुण्यफलं चाग्र्यं श्रृणु बुद्धिमतां वर ॥ 39.59 ॥
39.m: Whosoever performs the observance of Dharaṇī by this rite— / hear the foremost fruit of his merit, O best of the wise!

39.s:
yadi vaktrasahastrāṇi bhavanti mama suvrata .
āyuśca brahmaṇastulyaṃ bhaved yadi mahāvrata .. 39.60 ..
39.d:
यदि वक्त्रसहस्त्राणि भवन्ति मम सुव्रत ।
आयुश्च ब्रह्मणस्तुल्यं भवेद् यदि महाव्रत ॥ 39.60 ॥
39.m: Even if I had thousands of mouths, O you of noble vows, / and if my lifespan were equal to Brahmā's, O performer of great vows,

39.s:
tadānīmasya dharmasya phalaṃ kathayituṃ bhavet .
tathāpyuddeśato brahman kathayāmi śrṛṇuṣva tat .. 39.61 ..
39.d:
तदानीमस्य धर्मस्य फलं कथयितुं भवेत् ।
तथाप्युद्देशतो ब्रह्मन् कथयामि श्रृणुष्व तत् ॥ 39.61 ॥
39.m: only then would it be possible to declare the fruit of this religious duty. / Nevertheless, O brāhmaṇa, I shall declare it in outline; listen to that!

39.s:
daśa sapta daśa dve ca aṣṭau catvāra eva ca .
lakṣāyutāni catvāri ekasthaṃ syāccaturyugam .. 39.62 ..
39.d:
दश सप्त दश द्वे च अष्टौ चत्वार एव च ।
लक्षायुतानि चत्वारि एकस्थं स्याच्चतुर्युगम् ॥ 39.62 ॥
39.m: Ten, seven, ten, and two, and eight, and four— / forty-three hundred-thousands [combined] together make one four-age cycle.

39.s:
tairekasaptatiyugaṃ bhavenmanvantaraṃ mune .
caturdaśāho brāhmastu tāvatī rātririṣyate .. 39.63 ..
39.d:
तैरेकसप्ततियुगं भवेन्मन्वन्तरं मुने ।
चतुर्दशाहो ब्राह्मस्तु तावती रात्रिरिष्यते ॥ 39.63 ॥
39.m: Seventy-one of those ages make one manvantara, O sage. / Fourteen [manvantaras] are a day of Brahmā, and a night of equal length is acknowledged.

39.s:
evaṃ triṃśaddino māsaste dvādaśa samā smṛtā .
teṣāṃ śataṃ brahmaṇastu āyurnāstyatra saṃśayaḥ .. 39.64 ..
39.d:
एवं त्रिंशद्दिनो मासस्ते द्वादश समा स्मृता ।
तेषां शतं ब्रह्मणस्तु आयुर्नास्त्यत्र संशयः ॥ 39.64 ॥
39.m: Thus thirty days make a month; twelve of those are known as a year. / One hundred of those is the lifespan of Brahmā; there is no doubt about this.

39.s:
yaḥ sakṛd dvādaśīmetāmanena vidhinā kṣipet .
sa brahmalokamāpnoti tatkālaṃ caiva tiṣṭhati .. 39.65 ..
39.d:
यः सकृद् द्वादशीमेतामनेन विधिना क्षिपेत् ।
स ब्रह्मलोकमाप्नोति तत्कालं चैव तिष्ठति ॥ 39.65 ॥
39.m: Whoever passes this twelfth lunar day just once according to this rite, / he attains the world of Brahmā and remains there for that duration.

39.s:
tato brahmopasaṃhāre tallayaṃ tiṣṭhate ciram .
punaḥ sṛṣṭau bhaved devo vairājānāṃ mahātapāḥ .. 39.66 ..
39.d:
ततो ब्रह्मोपसंहारे तल्लयं तिष्ठते चिरम् ।
पुनः सृष्टौ भवेद् देवो वैराजानां महातपाः ॥ 39.66 ॥
39.m: Then, at the cosmic dissolution of Brahmā, he remains merged therein for a long time; / at the new creation, he becomes a god of the Vairājas, possessed of great ascetic power.

39.s:
brahmahatyādipāpāni iha lokakṛtānyapi .
akāme kāmato vāpi tāni naśyanti tatkṣaṇāt .. 39.67 ..
39.d:
ब्रह्महत्यादिपापानि इह लोककृतान्यपि ।
अकामे कामतो वापि तानि नश्यन्ति तत्क्षणात् ॥ 39.67 ॥
39.m: Sins such as killing a brāhmaṇa, even if committed in this world, / whether unintentionally or intentionally, perish in an instant.

39.s:
iha loke daridro yo bhraṣṭarājyo'tha vā nṛpaḥ .
upoṣya tāṃ vidhānena sa rājā jāyate dhruvam .. 39.68 ..
39.d:
इह लोके दरिद्रो यो भ्रष्टराज्योऽथ वा नृपः ।
उपोष्य तां विधानेन स राजा जायते ध्रुवम् ॥ 39.68 ॥
39.m: Whoever is poor in this world, or a king fallen from his kingdom, / fasting on that [tithi] according to the rite, he surely becomes a king.

39.s:
vandhyā nārī bhaved yā tu anena vidhinā śubhā .
upoṣyati bhavet tasyāḥ putraḥ paramadhārmikaḥ .. 39.69 ..
39.d:
वन्ध्या नारी भवेद् या तु अनेन विधिना शुभा ।
उपोष्यति भवेत् तस्याः पुत्रः परमधार्मिकः ॥ 39.69 ॥
39.m: Any auspicious woman who may be barren, / if she fasts according to this rite, she will obtain a son who is exceedingly righteous.

39.s:
agamyāgamanaṃ yena kṛtaṃ jānāti mānavaḥ .
sa imaṃ vidhimāsādya tasmāt pāpād vimucyate .. 39.70 ..
39.d:
अगम्यागमनं येन कृतं जानाति मानवः ।
स इमं विधिमासाद्य तस्मात् पापाद् विमुच्यते ॥ 39.70 ॥
39.m: A person who knows that he has approached a forbidden woman— / he, undertaking this rite, is freed from that sin.

39.s:
brahmakriyāyā lopena bahuvarṣakṛtena ca .
upoṣyemāṃ sakṛd bhaktyā vedasaṃskāramāpnuyāt .. 39.71 ..
39.d:
ब्रह्मक्रियाया लोपेन बहुवर्षकृतेन च ।
उपोष्येमां सकृद् भक्त्या वेदसंस्कारमाप्नुयात् ॥ 39.71 ॥
39.m: Even if Brahminical rites have been neglected for many years, / by fasting on this [tithi] just once with devotion, one attains the Vedic sacraments.

39.s:
kimatra bahunoktena na tadasti mahāmune .
aprāpyaṃ prāpyate naiva pāpaṃ vā yanna naśyati .. 39.72 ..
39.d:
किमत्र बहुनोक्तेन न तदस्ति महामुने ।
अप्राप्यं प्राप्यते नैव पापं वा यन्न नश्यति ॥ 39.72 ॥
39.m: What is the use of speaking much here? There is nothing, O great sage, / that is unobtainable which is not obtained, or any sin that does not perish.

39.s:
anena vidhinā brahman svayameva hyupoṣitā .
dharaṇyā magnayā tāta nātra kāryā vicāraṇā .. 39.73 ..
39.d:
अनेन विधिना ब्रह्मन् स्वयमेव ह्युपोषिता ।
धरण्या मग्नया तात नात्र कार्या विचारणा ॥ 39.73 ॥
39.m: By this rite, O brāhmaṇa, [the fast] was observed by Dharaṇī herself / when she was submerged, my dear; there should be no doubt here.

39.s:
adīkṣitāya no deyaṃ vidhānaṃ nāstikāya ca .
devabrahmadviṣe vā'pi na śrāvyaṃ tu kadācana .
gurubhaktāya dātavyaṃ sadyaḥ pāpapraṇāśanam .. 39.74 ..
39.d:
अदीक्षिताय नो देयं विधानं नास्तिकाय च ।
देवब्रह्मद्विषे वाऽपि न श्राव्यं तु कदाचन ।
गुरुभक्ताय दातव्यं सद्यः पापप्रणाशनम् ॥ 39.74 ॥
39.m: This procedure should not be given to the uninitiated, nor to an atheist, / nor should it ever be recited to one who hates gods and Brahmā; / it should be given to one devoted to the guru, instantly destroying sins.

39.s:
iha janmani saubhāgyaṃ dhanaṃ dhānyaṃ varastriyaḥ .
bhavanti vividhā yastu upoṣya vidhinā tataḥ .. 39.75 ..
39.d:
इह जन्मनि सौभाग्यं धनं धान्यं वरस्त्रियः ।
भवन्ति विविधा यस्तु उपोष्य विधिना ततः ॥ 39.75 ॥
39.m: Good fortune, wealth, grain, and excellent women / of various kinds are attained in this birth by one who fasts according to the rite.

39.s:
ya imaṃ śrāvayed bhaktyā dvādaśīkalpamuttamam .
śrṛṇoti vā sa pāpaistu sarvaireva pramucyate .. 39.76 ..
39.d:
य इमं श्रावयेद् भक्त्या द्वादशीकल्पमुत्तमम् ।
श्रृणोति वा स पापैस्तु सर्वैरेव प्रमुच्यते ॥ 39.76 ॥
39.m: Whoever recites this excellent rule for the twelfth lunar day with devotion, / or hears it, is completely freed from all sins.

39.s: .. iti śrīvarāhapurāṇe bhagavacchāstre ūnacatvāriṃśo'dhyāyaḥ .. 39 ..
39.d: ॥ इति श्रीवराहपुराणे भगवच्छास्त्रे ऊनचत्वारिंशोऽध्यायः ॥ 39 ॥
39.m: Thus ends the thirty-ninth chapter in the glorious Varāha Purāṇa, a scripture of the Lord.

40.s:
durvāsā uvāca .
tathaiva pauṣamāse tu amṛtaṃ mathitaṃ suraiḥ .
tatra kūrmo bhaved devaḥ svayameva janārdanaḥ .. 40.1 ..
40.d:
दुर्वासा उवाच ।
तथैव पौषमासे तु अमृतं मथितं सुरैः ।
तत्र कूर्मो भवेद् देवः स्वयमेव जनार्दनः ॥ 40.1 ॥
40.m: Durvāsas said: / Just so, in the month of Pauṣa, the nectar was churned by the gods; / there the god Janārdana became the Tortoise himself.

40.s:
tasyeyaṃ tithiruddiṣṭā harervai kūrmarūpiṇaḥ .
puṣyamāsasya yā śuddhā dvādaśī śuklapakṣataḥ .. 40.2 ..
40.d:
तस्येयं तिथिरुद्दिष्टा हरेर्वै कूर्मरूपिणः ।
पुष्यमासस्य या शुद्धा द्वादशी शुक्लपक्षतः ॥ 40.2 ॥
40.m: This lunar day is prescribed for Hari in the form of the Tortoise: / the bright twelfth lunar day belonging to the light fortnight of the month of Puṣya.

40.s:
tasyāṃ prāgeva saṃkalpya prāgvat snānnādikāḥ kriyāḥ .
nirvartyārādhayed rātryāmekādaśyāṃ janārdanam .
pṛthaṅmantrairmuniśreṣṭha devadevaṃ janārdanam .. 40.3 ..
40.d:
तस्यां प्रागेव संकल्प्य प्राग्वत् स्नान्नादिकाः क्रियाः ।
निर्वर्त्याराधयेद् रात्र्यामेकादश्यां जनार्दनम् ।
पृथङ्मन्त्रैर्मुनिश्रेष्ठ देवदेवं जनार्दनम् ॥ 40.3 ॥
40.m: Having made the solemn resolve beforehand on that day, and having performed / rites such as bathing as before, one should worship Janārdana at night on the eleventh lunar day, / with distinct mantras, O best of sages, [worshipping] Janārdana, the god of gods:

40.s:
oṃkūrmāya pādau prathamaṃ prapūjya
nārāyaṇeti hareḥ kaṭiṃ ca .
saṃkarṣaṇāyetyudaraṃ viśoke-
tyurobhavāyeti tathaiva kaṇṭham .
subāhavetyeva bhujau śiraśca
namo viśālāya rathāṅgasāram .. 40.4 ..
40.d:
ओंकूर्माय पादौ प्रथमं प्रपूज्य
नारायणेति हरेः कटिं च ।
संकर्षणायेत्युदरं विशोके-
त्युरोभवायेति तथैव कण्ठम् ।
सुबाहवेत्येव भुजौ शिरश्च
नमो विशालाय रथाङ्गसारम् ॥ 40.4 ॥
40.m: First worshipping the feet with “Oṃ, to the Tortoise,” / and Hari's waist with “To Nārāyaṇa,” / the belly with “To Saṃkarṣaṇa,” the chest with “To the Sorrowless One,” / and likewise the neck with “To the One Born of the Chest,” / the two arms with “To the One with Beautiful Arms,” and the head / and the essence of the discus with “Homage to the Vast One.”

40.s:
svanāmamantreṇa sugandhapuṣpai-
rnānānivedyairvividhaiḥ phalaiśca .
abhyarcya devaṃ kalaśaṃ tadagre
saṃsthāpya mālyaiḥ sitakaṇṭhadāma .. 40.5 ..
40.d:
स्वनाममन्त्रेण सुगन्धपुष्पै-
र्नानानिवेद्यैर्विविधैः फलैश्च ।
अभ्यर्च्य देवं कलशं तदग्रे
संस्थाप्य माल्यैः सितकण्ठदाम ॥ 40.5 ॥
40.m: Having worshipped the god with the mantra of his own name, with fragrant flowers, / with diverse offerings of food, and with various fruits, / placing a water jar before him with garlands, [binding] a white neck-band,

40.s:
taṃ ratnagarbhaṃ tu pureva kṛtvā
svaśaktito hemamayaṃ tu devam .
samandaraṃ kūrmarūpeṇa kṛtvā
saṃsthāpya tāmre ghṛtapūrṇapātre .
pūrṇaghaṭasyopari saṃniveśya
śvo brāhmaṇāyaivamevaṃ tu dadyāt .. 40.6 ..
40.d:
तं रत्नगर्भं तु पुरेव कृत्वा
स्वशक्तितो हेममयं तु देवम् ।
समन्दरं कूर्मरूपेण कृत्वा
संस्थाप्य ताम्रे घृतपूर्णपात्रे ।
पूर्णघटस्योपरि संनिवेश्य
श्वो ब्राह्मणायैवमेवं तु दद्यात् ॥ 40.6 ॥
40.m: filling it with jewels as before, and having made the god of gold according to one's capacity, / along with Mandara in the form of the Tortoise, / placing it in a copper vessel filled with ghee, / and depositing it on top of a full jar, he should give it to a brāhmaṇa the next day in this very manner.

40.s:
śvo brāhmaṇān bhojya sadakṣiṇāṃśca
yathāśaktyā prīṇayed devadevam .
nārāyaṇaṃ kūrmarūpeṇa paścād
tathā svayaṃ bhuñjīta sabhṛtyavargaḥ .. 40.7 ..
40.d:
श्वो ब्राह्मणान् भोज्य सदक्षिणांश्च
यथाशक्त्या प्रीणयेद् देवदेवम् ।
नारायणं कूर्मरूपेण पश्चाद्
तथा स्वयं भुञ्जीत सभृत्यवर्गः ॥ 40.7 ॥
40.m: Having fed brāhmaṇas the next day, along with monetary gifts, / he should propitiate according to his capacity the god of gods, / Nārāyaṇa in the form of the Tortoise; afterwards, / he himself should eat in that manner along with his group of servants.

40.s:
evaṃ kṛte vipra samastapāpaṃ
vinaśyate nātra kuryād vicāram .
saṃsāracakraṃ tu vihāya śuddhaṃ
prāpnoti lokaṃ ca hareḥ purāṇam .
prayānti pāpāni vināśamāśu
śrīmāṃstathā jāyate satyadharmaḥ .. 40.8 ..
40.d:
एवं कृते विप्र समस्तपापं
विनश्यते नात्र कुर्याद् विचारम् ।
संसारचक्रं तु विहाय शुद्धं
प्राप्नोति लोकं च हरेः पुराणम् ।
प्रयान्ति पापानि विनाशमाशु
श्रीमांस्तथा जायते सत्यधर्मः ॥ 40.8 ॥
40.m: When this is done, O brāhmaṇa, all sin / is destroyed—one should not doubt this. / Leaving behind the cycle of saṃsāra, he attains the pure / and ancient realm of Hari; / his sins quickly go to destruction, / and he becomes prosperous and one of true righteousness.

40.s:
anekajanmāntarasaṃcitāni
naśyanti pāpāni narasya bhaktyā .
prāguktarūpaṃ tu phalaṃ bhaveta
nārāyaṇastuṣṭimāyāti sadyaḥ .. 40.9 ..
40.d:
अनेकजन्मान्तरसंचितानि
नश्यन्ति पापानि नरस्य भक्त्या ।
प्रागुक्तरूपं तु फलं भवेत
नारायणस्तुष्टिमायाति सद्यः ॥ 40.9 ॥
40.m: Sins accumulated across many other births / perish through a man's devotion. / The fruit described earlier indeed comes to pass, / and Nārāyaṇa instantly attains satisfaction.
Thus ends the fortieth chapter in the glorious Varāha Purāṇa, a scripture of the Lord.

41.s:
durvāsā uvāca .
evaṃ māghe site pakṣe dvādaśīṃ dharaṇībhṛtaḥ .
varāhasya śrṛṇuṣvādyāṃ mune paramadhārmika .. 41.1 ..
41.d:
दुर्वासा उवाच ।
एवं माघे सिते पक्षे द्वादशीं धरणीभृतः ।
वराहस्य श्रृणुष्वाद्यां मुने परमधार्मिक ॥ 41.1 ॥
41.m: Durvāsas said: / Hear now, O most righteous sage, about the primary twelfth lunar day / of the Boar, the bearer of Dharaṇī, in the bright fortnight of Māgha.

41.s:
prāguktena vidhānena saṃkalpasnānameva ca .
kṛtvā devaṃ samabhyarcya ekādaśyāṃ vicakṣaṇaḥ .. 41.2 ..
41.d:
प्रागुक्तेन विधानेन संकल्पस्नानमेव च ।
कृत्वा देवं समभ्यर्च्य एकादश्यां विचक्षणः ॥ 41.2 ॥
41.m: Having performed the solemn resolve and the bath / according to the rite stated earlier, and having worshipped the god on the eleventh lunar day, the wise man,

41.s:
dhūpanaivedyagandhaiśca arcayitvā'cyutaṃ naraḥ .
paścāt tasyāgrataḥ kumbhaṃ jalapūrṇaṃ tu vinyaset .. 41.3 ..
41.d:
धूपनैवेद्यगन्धैश्च अर्चयित्वाऽच्युतं नरः ।
पश्चात् तस्याग्रतः कुम्भं जलपूर्णं तु विन्यसेत् ॥ 41.3 ॥
41.m: having worshipped Acyuta with incense, food offerings, and fragrances, / should then place before him a water jar filled with water.

41.s:
oṃ vārāhāyeti pādau tu mādhavāyeti vai kaṭim .
kṣetrajñāyeti jaṭharaṃ viśvarūpetyuro hareḥ .. 41.4 ..
41.d:
ओं वाराहायेति पादौ तु माधवायेति वै कटिम् ।
क्षेत्रज्ञायेति जठरं विश्वरूपेत्युरो हरेः ॥ 41.4 ॥
41.m: The feet [are worshipped] with “Oṃ, to the Boar,” the waist with “To Mādhava,” / the belly with “To the Knower of the Field,” the chest of Hari with “To the Universal Form,”

41.s:
sarvajñāyeti kaṇṭhaṃ tu prajānāṃ pataye śiraḥ .
pradyumnāyeti ca bhujau divyāstrāya sudarśanam .
amṛtodbhavāya śaṅkhaṃ tu eṣa devārcane vidhiḥ .. 41.5 ..
41.d:
सर्वज्ञायेति कण्ठं तु प्रजानां पतये शिरः ।
प्रद्युम्नायेति च भुजौ दिव्यास्त्राय सुदर्शनम् ।
अमृतोद्भवाय शङ्खं तु एष देवार्चने विधिः ॥ 41.5 ॥
41.m: the neck with “To the Omniscient,” the head with “To the Lord of Creatures,” / the two arms with “To Pradyumna,” the Sudarśana discus with “To the Divine Weapon,” / and the conch with “To the One Arisen from Nectar”—this is the rite for worshipping the god.

41.s:
evamabhyarcya medhāvī tasmin kumbhe tu vinyaset .
sauvarṇaṃ raupyatāmraṃ vā pātraṃ vibhavaśaktitaḥ .. 41.6 ..
41.d:
एवमभ्यर्च्य मेधावी तस्मिन् कुम्भे तु विन्यसेत् ।
सौवर्णं रौप्यताम्रं वा पात्रं विभवशक्तितः ॥ 41.6 ॥
41.m: Having worshipped thus, the wise man should place upon that jar / a gold, silver, or copper vessel according to his wealth and capacity.

41.s:
sarvabījaistu saṃpūrṇaṃ sthāpayitvā vicakṣaṇaḥ .
tatra śaktyā tu sauvarṇaṃ vārāhaṃ kārayed budhaḥ .. 41.7 ..
41.d:
सर्वबीजैस्तु संपूर्णं स्थापयित्वा विचक्षणः ।
तत्र शक्त्या तु सौवर्णं वाराहं कारयेद् बुधः ॥ 41.7 ॥
41.m: Filling [the vessel] with all kinds of seeds, the discerning person should place it [there]; / and there, according to his capacity, the wise man should have a golden image of Varāha made, 41.7

41.s:
daṃṣṭrāgreṇoddhṛtāṃ pṛthvīṃ saparvatavanadrumām .
mādhavaṃ madhuhantāraṃ vārāhaṃ rūpamāsthitam .. 41.8 ..
41.d:
दंष्ट्राग्रेणोद्धृतां पृथ्वीं सपर्वतवनद्रुमाम् ।
माधवं मधुहन्तारं वाराहं रूपमास्थितम् ॥ 41.8 ॥
41.m: [representing] the Earth, with her mountains, forests, and trees, lifted up by the tip of his tusk— / Mādhava, the slayer of Madhu, who assumed the form of a boar. 41.8

41.s:
sarvabījabhṛte pātre ratnagarbhaṃ ghaṭopari .
sthāpayet paramaṃ devaṃ jātarūpamayaṃ harim .. 41.9 ..
41.d:
सर्वबीजभृते पात्रे रत्नगर्भं घटोपरि ।
स्थापयेत् परमं देवं जातरूपमयं हरिम् ॥ 41.9 ॥
41.m: On the vessel filled with all seeds, upon the jar containing jewels, / he should place the supreme deity, Hari, fashioned of gold. 41.9

41.s:
sitavastrayugacchannaṃ tāmrapātraṃ tu vai mune .
sthāpyārccayed gandhapuṣpairnaivedyairvividhaiḥ śubhaiḥ .. 41.10 ..
41.d:
सितवस्त्रयुगच्छन्नं ताम्रपात्रं तु वै मुने ।
स्थाप्यार्च्चयेद् गन्धपुष्पैर्नैवेद्यैर्विविधैः शुभैः ॥ 41.10 ॥
41.m: Covering the copper vessel with a pair of white garments, O sage, / he should set it down and worship it with fragrant perfumes, flowers, and various auspicious food offerings. 41.10

41.s:
puṣpamaṇḍalikāṃ kṛtvā jāgaraṃ tatra kārayet .
prādurbhāvān harestatra vācayed bhāvayed budhaḥ .. 41.11 ..
41.d:
पुष्पमण्डलिकां कृत्वा जागरं तत्र कारयेत् ।
प्रादुर्भावान् हरेस्तत्र वाचयेद् भावयेद् बुधः ॥ 41.11 ॥
41.m: Having arranged a circular garland of flowers, he should keep a night vigil there; / the wise man should read aloud and contemplate there the manifestations of Hari. 41.11

41.s:
evaṃ sanniyamasyāntaṃ prabhāte udite ravau .
śuciḥ snātvā hariṃ pūjya brāhmaṇāya nivedayet .. 41.12 ..
41.d:
एवं सन्नियमस्यान्तं प्रभाते उदिते रवौ ।
शुचिः स्नात्वा हरिं पूज्य ब्राह्मणाय निवेदयेत् ॥ 41.12 ॥
41.m: Thus, at the conclusion of his vow, at dawn when the sun has risen, / having bathed and become pure, and having worshipped Hari, he should present it to a brāhmaṇa. 41.12

41.s:
vedavedāṅgaviduṣe sādhuvṛttāya dhīmate .
viṣṇubhaktāya viprarṣe viśeṣeṇa pradāpayet .. 41.13 ..
41.d:
वेदवेदाङ्गविदुषे साधुवृत्ताय धीमते ।
विष्णुभक्ताय विप्रर्षे विशेषेण प्रदापयेत् ॥ 41.13 ॥
41.m: To one learned in the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, of virtuous conduct and wise, / devoted to Viṣṇu, O brāhmaṇa-sage, he should give it especially. 41.13

41.s:
devaṃ sakumbhaṃ taṃ dattvā hariṃ vārāharūpiṇam .
brāhmaṇāya bhaved yaddhi phalaṃ tanme niśāmaya .. 41.14 ..
41.d:
देवं सकुम्भं तं दत्त्वा हरिं वाराहरूपिणम् ।
ब्राह्मणाय भवेद् यद्धि फलं तन्मे निशामय ॥ 41.14 ॥
41.m: When he has given that deity along with the jar—Hari in the form of a boar— / to a brāhmaṇa, hear from me the fruit that comes to pass: 41.14

41.s:
iha janmani saubhāgyaṃ śrīḥ kāntistuṣṭireva ca .
daridro vittavān sadyaḥ aputro labhate sutam .
alakṣmīrnaśyate sadyo lakṣmīḥ saṃviśate kṣaṇāt .. 41.15 ..
41.d:
इह जन्मनि सौभाग्यं श्रीः कान्तिस्तुष्टिरेव च ।
दरिद्रो वित्तवान् सद्यः अपुत्रो लभते सुतम् ।
अलक्ष्मीर्नश्यते सद्यो लक्ष्मीः संविशते क्षणात् ॥ 41.15 ॥
41.m: good fortune in this life, prosperity, beauty, and contentment; / a poor man straightaway becomes wealthy, a childless man obtains a son, / misfortune is at once destroyed, and fortune enters in a moment. 41.15

41.s:
iha janmani saubhāgyaṃ paraloke niśāmaya .
asminnarthe purāvṛttamitihāsaṃ purātanam .. 41.16 ..
41.d:
इह जन्मनि सौभाग्यं परलोके निशामय ।
अस्मिन्नर्थे पुरावृत्तमितिहासं पुरातनम् ॥ 41.16 ॥
41.m: [Such is] good fortune in this life; hear of [the fruit in] the next world. / In this connection [is told] an ancient narrative of an event of the past: 41.16

41.s:
iha loke'bhavad rājā vīradhanveti viśrutaḥ .
sa kadācid vanaṃ prāyān mṛgahetoḥ paraṃtapaḥ .. 41.17 ..
41.d:
इह लोकेऽभवद् राजा वीरधन्वेति विश्रुतः ।
स कदाचिद् वनं प्रायान् मृगहेतोः परंतपः ॥ 41.17 ॥
41.m: In this world there was a king renowned as Vīradhanvan; / once that scorcher of foes went to the forest for the sake of deer. 41.17

41.s:
vyāpādayan mṛgagaṇān tatrarṣivanamadhyagaḥ .
jaghāna mṛgarūpān so'jñānato brāhmaṇān nṛpaḥ .. 41.18 ..
41.d:
व्यापादयन् मृगगणान् तत्रर्षिवनमध्यगः ।
जघान मृगरूपान् सोऽज्ञानतो ब्राह्मणान् नृपः ॥ 41.18 ॥
41.m: Slaying herds of deer, while in the midst of a sages' forest / that king unknowingly killed brāhmaṇas who had the form of deer. 41.18

41.s:
bhrātarastatra pañcāśanmṛgarūpeṇa saṃsthitāḥ .
saṃvartasya sutā brahman vedādhyayanatatparāḥ .. 41.19 ..
41.d:
भ्रातरस्तत्र पञ्चाशन्मृगरूपेण संस्थिताः ।
संवर्तस्य सुता ब्रह्मन् वेदाध्ययनतत्पराः ॥ 41.19 ॥
41.m: There were fifty brothers staying there in the form of deer, / the sons of Saṃvarta, O sage, intent on the study of the Vedas. 41.19

41.s:
satyatapā uvāca .
kāraṇaṃ kiṃ samāśritya te cakrurmṛgarūpatām .
etanme kautukaṃ brahman praṇatasya prasīda me .. 41.20 ..
41.d:
सत्यतपा उवाच ।
कारणं किं समाश्रित्य ते चक्रुर्मृगरूपताम् ।
एतन्मे कौतुकं ब्रह्मन् प्रणतस्य प्रसीद मे ॥ 41.20 ॥
41.m: Satyatapas said: / Depending on what cause did they take on the form of deer? / This is my curiosity, O sage; be gracious to me who am bowed before you. 41.20

41.s:
durvāsā uvāca .
te kadācid vanaṃ yātā dṛṣṭvā hariṇapotakān .
jātamātrān svamātrā tu vihīnān dṛśya sattama .
ekaikaṃ jagṛhuste hi te mṛtāḥ skandhasaṃsthitāḥ .. 41.21 ..
41.d:
दुर्वासा उवाच ।
ते कदाचिद् वनं याता दृष्ट्वा हरिणपोतकान् ।
जातमात्रान् स्वमात्रा तु विहीनान् दृश्य सत्तम ।
एकैकं जगृहुस्ते हि ते मृताः स्कन्धसंस्थिताः ॥ 41.21 ॥
41.m: Durvāsas said: / Once, going to the forest and seeing fawns / that were newborn and bereft of their mother, O best of men, / they each picked up one, and those [fawns] died while on their shoulders. 41.21

41.s:
tataste duḥkhitāḥ sarve yayuḥ pitaramantikam .
ūcuśca vacanaṃ cedaṃ mṛgahiṃsāmṛte mune .. 41.22 ..
41.d:
ततस्ते दुःखिताः सर्वे ययुः पितरमन्तिकम् ।
ऊचुश्च वचनं चेदं मृगहिंसामृते मुने ॥ 41.22 ॥
41.m: Then, all grief-stricken, they went to their father's presence, / and spoke these words regarding the unintended killing of deer, O sage: 41.22

41.s:
ṛṣiputrakā ūcuḥ .
jātamātrā mṛgāḥ pañca asmābhirnihatā mune .
akāmatastato'smākaṃ prāyaścittaṃ vidhīyatām .. 41.23 ..
41.d:
ऋषिपुत्रका ऊचुः ।
जातमात्रा मृगाः पञ्च अस्माभिर्निहता मुने ।
अकामतस्ततोऽस्माकं प्रायश्चित्तं विधीयताम् ॥ 41.23 ॥
41.m: The sage's sons said: / Five newborn deer were killed by us, O sage, / unintentionally; therefore, let an expiation be prescribed for us. 41.23

41.s:
saṃvartta uvāca .
matpitā hiṃsakastvāsīdahaṃ tasmād viśeṣataḥ .
bhavantaḥ pāpakarmāṇaḥ saṃjātā mama putrakāḥ .. 41.24 ..
41.d:
संवर्त्त उवाच ।
मत्पिता हिंसकस्त्वासीदहं तस्माद् विशेषतः ।
भवन्तः पापकर्माणः संजाता मम पुत्रकाः ॥ 41.24 ॥
41.m: Saṃvarta said: / My father was indeed a slayer, and I even more so; / you, my sons, have been born as evildoers. 41.24

41.s:
idānīṃ mṛgacarmāṇi paridhāya yatavratāḥ .
caraghvaṃ pañcavarṣāṇi tataḥ śuddhā bhaviṣyatha .. 41.25 ..
41.d:
इदानीं मृगचर्माणि परिधाय यतव्रताः ।
चरघ्वं पञ्चवर्षाणि ततः शुद्धा भविष्यथ ॥ 41.25 ॥
41.m: Now, wearing deer-skins and keeping vows, / wander for five years; then you will become purified. 41.25

41.s:
evamuktāstu te putrā mṛgacarmopavītinaḥ .
vanaṃ viviśuravyagrā japanto brahma śāśvatam .. 41.26 ..
41.d:
एवमुक्तास्तु ते पुत्रा मृगचर्मोपवीतिनः ।
वनं विविशुरव्यग्रा जपन्तो ब्रह्म शाश्वतम् ॥ 41.26 ॥
41.m: Thus addressed, those sons, wearing deer-skins as sacred threads, / entered the forest undistracted, reciting the eternal Brahman. 41.26

41.s:
tathā varṣe vyatikrānte vīradhanvā mahīpatiḥ .
tatrājagāma yasmiṃste caranti mṛgarūpiṇaḥ .. 41.27 ..
41.d:
तथा वर्षे व्यतिक्रान्ते वीरधन्वा महीपतिः ।
तत्राजगाम यस्मिंस्ते चरन्ति मृगरूपिणः ॥ 41.27 ॥
41.m: When a year had thus passed, King Vīradhanvan / came there where they were wandering in the appearance of deer. 41.27

41.s:
te cāpyekatarormūle mṛgacarmmopavītinaḥ .
japantaḥ saṃsthitāste hi rājñā dṛṣṭvā mṛgā iti .
matvā viddhāstu yugapanmṛtāste brahmavādinaḥ .. 41.28 ..
41.d:
ते चाप्येकतरोर्मूले मृगचर्म्मोपवीतिनः ।
जपन्तः संस्थितास्ते हि राज्ञा दृष्ट्वा मृगा इति ।
मत्वा विद्धास्तु युगपन्मृतास्ते ब्रह्मवादिनः ॥ 41.28 ॥
41.m: And they, wearing deer-skins as sacred threads, / were staying at the foot of a tree, reciting [sacred texts]; the king, seeing them, / thought, 'They are deer,' and pierced them simultaneously; and those teachers of the Veda died. 41.28

41.s:
tān dṛṣṭvā tu mṛtān rājā brāhmaṇān saṃśitavratān .
bhayena vepamānastu devarātāśramaṃ yayau .
tatrāpṛcchad brahmavadhyā mamāyātā mahāmune .. 41.29 ..
41.d:
तान् दृष्ट्वा तु मृतान् राजा ब्राह्मणान् संशितव्रतान् ।
भयेन वेपमानस्तु देवराताश्रमं ययौ ।
तत्रापृच्छद् ब्रह्मवध्या ममायाता महामुने ॥ 41.29 ॥
41.m: Seeing those brāhmaṇas of rigorous vows dead, / the king, trembling with fear, went to the hermitage of Devarāta; / there he asked, 'The killing of a brāhmaṇa has come upon me, O great sage!' 41.29

41.s:
āmūlya tad vadhaṃ vṛttaṃ kathayitvā narādhipaḥ .
bhṛśaṃ śokaparītātmā ruroda bhṛśaduḥkhitaḥ .. 41.30 ..
41.d:
आमूल्य तद् वधं वृत्तं कथयित्वा नराधिपः ।
भृशं शोकपरीतात्मा रुरोद भृशदुःखितः ॥ 41.30 ॥
41.m: Having related the whole event of that killing from the beginning, the ruler of men, / his heart completely overcome with sorrow, wept in deep distress. 41.30

41.s:
sa ṛṣirdevarātastu rudantaṃ nṛpasattamam .
uvāca mā bhairnṛpate apaneṣyāmi pātakam .. 41.31 ..
41.d:
स ऋषिर्देवरातस्तु रुदन्तं नृपसत्तमम् ।
उवाच मा भैर्नृपते अपनेष्यामि पातकम् ॥ 41.31 ॥
41.m: That sage Devarāta said to the best of kings / who was weeping: 'Do not fear, O king! I shall remove the sin. 41.31

41.s:
pātāle sutalākhye ca yathā dhātrī nimajjatī .
uddhṛtā devadevena viṣṇunā kroḍamūrttinā .. 41.32 ..
41.d:
पाताले सुतलाख्ये च यथा धात्री निमज्जती ।
उद्धृता देवदेवेन विष्णुना क्रोडमूर्त्तिना ॥ 41.32 ॥
